However, underlying or contributory mental disorders should be noted using the qualifier ‘Associated with psychological and behavioural factors, including mental disorders’, rather than using with this category.

HA40.1.title: Aetiological considerations associated with psychological or behavioural factors, including mental disorders
HA40.1.definition: This category should be assigned when psychological and behavioural factors or symptoms are important contributing factors to the Sexual Dysfunction or Sexual Pain Disorder. Examples include low self-esteem, negative attitudes toward sexual activity, adverse past sexual experiences, and behavioural patterns such as poor sleep hygiene and overwork. Depressive, anxiety, or cognitive symptoms as well as other symptoms of Mental, Behavioural, or Neurodevelopmental Disorders may also interfere with sexual functioning. If the symptoms reach the level of constituting a diagnosable Mental and Behavioural Disorder and the Sexual Dysfunction or Sexual Pain Disorder is an independent focus of clinical attention, this category should be used and the appropriate Mental and Behavioural Disorder diagnosis should also be assigned. However, underlying or contributory Disorders Due to Substance Use should be noted using the category ‘Associated with use of psychoactive substance or medication’, rather than using this category.

HA40.2.title: Aetiological considerations associated with use of psychoactive substance or medication
HA40.2.definition: This category should be assigned when there is evidence that the direct physiological effects of a psychoactive substance or medication are an important contributing factor to the Sexual Dysfunction or Sexual Pain Disorder. Examples include selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, histamine-2 receptor antagonists (e.g., cimetidine), alcohol, opioids, and amphetamines. If the diagnostic requirements for a Disorder Due to Substance Use are met, the appropriate Disorder Due to Substance Use diagnosis should also be assigned.

HA40.3.title: Aetiological considerations associated with lack of knowledge or experience
HA40.3.definition: This category should be assigned when, in the clinician’s judgment, the individual’s lack of knowledge or experience of her or his own body, sexual functioning, and sexual response is an important contributing factor to the Sexual Dysfunction or Sexual Pain Disorder. This includes inaccurate information or myths about sexual functioning.

HA40.4.title: Aetiological considerations associated with relationship factors
HA40.4.definition: This category should be assigned when, in the clinician’s judgment, relationship factors are important contributing factors to the Sexual Dysfunction or Sexual Pain Disorder. Examples include relationship conflict or lack of romantic attachment. This category may also be used when the Sexual Dysfunction or Sexual Pain Disorder is associated with a Sexual Dysfunction or Sexual Pain Disorder in the sexual partner.

HA40.5.title: Aetiological considerations associated with cultural factors
HA40.5.definition: This category should be assigned when, in the clinician’s judgment, cultural factors are important contributing factors to the Sexual Dysfunction or Sexual Pain Disorder. Cultural factors may influence expectations or provoke inhibitions about the experience of sexual pleasure or other aspects of sexual activity. Other examples include strong culturally shared beliefs about sexual expression, for example a belief that loss of semen can lead to weakness, disease or death.

HA60.title: Gender incongruence of adolescence or adulthood
HA60.definition: Gender Incongruence of Adolescence and Adulthood is characterised by a marked and persistent incongruence between an individual’s experienced gender and the assigned sex, which often leads to a desire to ‘transition’, in order to live and be accepted as a person of the experienced gender, through hormonal treatment, surgery or other health care services to make the individual’s body align, as much as desired and to the extent possible, with the experienced gender. The diagnosis cannot be assigned prior to the onset of puberty. Gender variant behaviour and preferences alone are not a basis for assigning the diagnosis.

HA61.title: Gender incongruence of childhood
HA61.definition: Gender incongruence of childhood is characterised by a marked incongruence between an individual’s experienced/expressed gender and the assigned sex in pre-pubertal children. It includes a strong desire to be a different gender than the assigned sex; a strong dislike on the child’s part of his or her sexual anatomy or anticipated secondary sex characteristics and/or a strong desire for the primary and/or anticipated secondary sex characteristics that match the experienced gender; and make-believe or fantasy play, toys, games, or activities and playmates that are typical of the experienced gender rather than the assigned sex. The incongruence must have persisted for about 2 years. Gender variant behaviour and preferences alone are not a basis for assigning the diagnosis.

JA00.0.title: Spontaneous abortion
JA00.0.definition: Spontaneous abortion (also referred to as miscarriage) is a spontaneous loss of pregnancy (i.e. embryo or fetus) before 22 completed weeks of gestation. When information on gestational age is unavailable, use birthweight less than 500 grams as the criteria. Spontaneous abortions (miscarriages) are distinct from cases of induced abortion.

JA00.00.title: Spontaneous abortion, incomplete, complicated by genital tract or pelvic infection
JA00.00.definition: A condition caused by immunological factors, abnormal ovum or uterine body, maternal disease or infection, or cervical incompetence and complicated by genital tract or pelvic infection. This condition is characterised by the incomplete passage of products of conception prior to 22 weeks gestation or weighing less than 500 grams.

JA00.01.title: Spontaneous abortion, incomplete, complicated by delayed or excessive haemorrhage
JA00.01.definition: A condition caused by immunological factors, abnormal ovum or uterine body, maternal disease or infection, or cervical incompetence and complicated by delayed or excessive bleeding. This condition is characterised by incomplete passage of products of conception prior to 22 weeks gestation or weighing less than 500 grams.

JA00.02.title: Spontaneous abortion, incomplete, complicated by embolism
JA00.02.definition: A condition caused by immunological factors, abnormal ovum or uterine body, maternal disease or infection, or cervical incompetence and complicated by embolism. This condition is characterised by incomplete passage of products of conception prior to 22 weeks gestation or weighing less than 500 grams.

JA00.03.title: Spontaneous abortion, incomplete, with other or unspecified complications

JA00.04.title: Spontaneous abortion, incomplete, without complication
JA00.04.definition: A condition caused by immunological factors, abnormal ovum or uterine body, maternal disease or infection, or cervical incompetence without any associated complications. This condition is characterised by incomplete passage of products of conception prior to 22 weeks gestation or weighing less than 500 grams.

JA00.05.title: Spontaneous abortion, complete or unspecified, complicated by genital tract or pelvic infection

JA00.06.title: Spontaneous abortion, complete or unspecified, complicated by delayed or excessive haemorrhage
JA00.06.definition: A condition caused by immunological factors, abnormal ovum or uterine body, maternal disease or infection, or cervical incompetence, and complicated by delayed or excessive bleeding. This condition is characterised by complete or unspecified non-induced embryonic or fetal death or passage of products of conception prior to 22 weeks' gestation or weighing less than 500 grams.

JA00.07.title: Spontaneous abortion, complete or unspecified, complicated by embolism
JA00.07.definition: A condition caused by immunological factors, abnormal ovum or uterine body, maternal disease or infection, or cervical incompetence, and complicated by embolism. This condition is characterised by complete or unspecified non-induced embryonic or fetal death or passage of products of conception prior to 22 weeks gestation or weighing less than 500 grams.

JA00.08.title: Spontaneous abortion, complete or unspecified, with other or unspecified complications

JA00.09.title: Spontaneous abortion, complete or unspecified, without complication

JA00.1.title: Induced abortion
JA00.1.definition: Induced abortion (also referred to as Artificial termination of pregnancy) is a complete expulsion or extraction from a woman of an embryo or a fetus (irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy), following a deliberate interruption of an ongoing pregnancy by medical or surgical means, which is not intended to result in a live birth. Induced abortions are distinct from cases of spontaneous abortion and stillbirth.

JA00.10.title: Induced abortion, incomplete, complicated by genital tract or pelvic infection

JA00.11.title: Induced abortion, incomplete, complicated by delayed or excessive haemorrhage

JA00.12.title: Induced abortion, incomplete, complicated by embolism

JA00.13.title: Induced abortion, incomplete, with other or unspecified complications

JA00.15.title: Induced abortion, complete or unspecified, complicated by genital tract or pelvic infection

JA00.16.title: Induced abortion, complete or unspecified, complicated by delayed or excessive haemorrhage
JA00.16.definition: A condition caused by surgical, pharmacological, mechanical, artificial, or other unspecified interventions and complicated by delayed or excessive bleeding. This condition is characterised by termination of pregnancy and intentional embryonic or fetal death with complete or unspecified expulsion of products of conception from the uterus before the fetus is viable.

JA00.17.title: Induced abortion, complete or unspecified, complicated by embolism
JA00.17.definition: A condition caused by surgical, pharmacological, mechanical, artificial, or other unspecified interventions and complicated by embolism. This condition is characterised by termination of pregnancy and intentional embryonic or fetal death with complete or unspecified expulsion of products of conception from the uterus before the fetus is viable.

JA00.18.title: Induced abortion, complete or unspecified, with other or unspecified complication

JA00.19.title: Induced abortion, complete or unspecified, without complication

JA00.20.title: Unspecified abortion, incomplete, complicated by genital tract or pelvic infection

JA00.21.title: Unspecified abortion, incomplete, complicated by delayed or excessive haemorrhage

JA00.22.title: Unspecified abortion, incomplete, complicated by embolism

JA00.23.title: Unspecified abortion, incomplete, with other or unspecified complications

JA00.25.title: Unspecified abortion, complete or unspecified, complicated by genital tract or pelvic infection

JA00.26.title: Unspecified abortion, complete or unspecified, complicated by delayed or excessive haemorrhage

JA00.27.title: Unspecified abortion, complete or unspecified, complicated by embolism

JA00.28.title: Unspecified abortion, complete or unspecified, with other or unspecified complications

JA00.29.title: Unspecified abortion, complete or unspecified, without complication

JA00.3.title: Failed attempted abortion
JA00.3.definition: Ongoing pregnancy after medical or surgical interventions which fail to terminate the pregnancy.

JA00.30.title: Failed medical abortion, complicated by genital tract or pelvic infection
JA00.30.definition: Medical interventions which fail to terminate the pregnancy and complicated by genital tract and pelvic infection

JA00.31.title: Failed medical abortion, complicated by delayed or excessive haemorrhage
JA00.31.definition: Medical interventions which fail to terminate the pregnancy and complicated by delayed or excessive haemorrhage

JA00.32.title: Failed medical abortion, complicated by embolism
JA00.32.definition: Medical interventions which fail to terminate the pregnancy and complicated by delayed or excessive haemorrhage

JA00.33.title: Failed medical abortion, with other or unspecified complications
JA00.33.definition: Medical interventions which fail to terminate the pregnancy and associated with other and unspecified complications.

JA00.34.title: Failed medical abortion, without complication
JA00.34.definition: Medical interventions which fail to terminate the pregnancy without any associated complications.

JA00.35.title: Other or unspecified failed attempted abortion, complicated by genital tract or pelvic infection

JA00.36.title: Other or unspecified failed attempted abortion, complicated by delayed or excessive haemorrhage

JA00.37.title: Other or unspecified failed attempted abortion, complicated by embolism

JA00.38.title: Other or unspecified failed attempted abortion, with other or unspecified complications

JA00.39.title: Other or unspecified failed attempted abortion, without complication

JA01.title: Ectopic pregnancy
JA01.definition: Any condition characterised by implantation of the embryo outside the endometrium and endometrial cavity during pregnancy.

JA01.0.title: Abdominal pregnancy
JA01.0.definition: A condition characterised by implantation of the embryo within the peritoneal cavity during pregnancy.

JA01.1.title: Tubal pregnancy
JA01.1.definition: A condition characterised by implantation of the embryo within the fallopian tube (ampullary, isthmus, interstitium) during pregnancy.

JA01.2.title: Ovarian pregnancy
JA01.2.definition: A condition characterised by implantation of the embryo within the ovary during pregnancy.

JA02.title: Molar pregnancy
JA02.definition: A condition caused by the over-production of cells arising into the placenta during pregnancy. This condition is characterised by a pregnancy with abnormal placental growth in which the chorionic villi become hydropic, trophoblast proliferation and invasion of the uterine tissue within 10-16 weeks after conception, and a placental mass.

JA02.0.title: Complete hydatidiform mole
JA02.0.definition: A condition caused by the over-production of cells arising into the placenta during pregnancy. This condition is characterised by a pregnancy with abnormal placental growth in which the chorionic villi become hydropic, slight to severe trophoblast proliferation and invasion of the uterine tissue within 10-16 weeks after conception, a placental mass, 25-30% theca lutein cysts, 15-20% persistent trophoblastic disease, 50% uterine size for dates, and vaginal bleeding, nausea, or vomiting. This condition leads to an absent fetus.

JA02.1.title: Incomplete or partial hydatidiform mole
JA02.1.definition: A condition caused by the over-production of cells arising into the placenta during pregnancy. This condition is characterised by a pregnancy with abnormal placental growth in which the chorionic villi become hydropic, slight to moderate trophoblast proliferation and invasion of the uterine tissue within 10-16 weeks after conception, a placental mass, theca lutein cysts, 1-5% persistent trophoblastic disease, small uterine size for dates, and vaginal bleeding, nausea, or vomiting. This condition leads to some fetal development and a missed abortion.

JA03.title: Missed abortion
JA03.definition: A condition caused by genetic abnormality, abnormal cell division, or poor quality ovum or sperm. This condition is characterised by a failed pregnancy, immature fetal or embryonic death that is not expelled from the uterus for at least 8 weeks, and diminished uterine size. This condition may also present with maternal infection, blood clotting, fetal calcification, and resorption of conception products. Confirmation is by imaging.

JA04.title: Blighted ovum or nonhydatidiform mole
JA04.definition: A condition caused by genetic abnormality, abnormal cell division, or poor quality ovum or sperm. This condition is characterised by a failed pregnancy, implantation of a fertilized egg without development into an embryo, haemorrhage into the decidua, and adjacent tissue necrosis.

JA05.title: Complications following abortion, ectopic or molar pregnancy
JA05.definition: Any complication affecting pregnant females, caused by or subsequent to abortion, ectopic, and molar pregnancy.

JA05.0.title: Genital tract or pelvic infection following abortion, ectopic or molar pregnancy

JA05.1.title: Delayed or excessive haemorrhage following abortion, ectopic or molar pregnancy

JA05.2.title: Embolism following abortion, ectopic or molar pregnancy

JA05.3.title: Shock following abortion, ectopic or molar pregnancy

JA05.4.title: Renal failure following abortion, ectopic or molar pregnancy

JA05.5.title: Metabolic disorders following abortion, ectopic or molar pregnancy

JA05.6.title: Damage to pelvic organs and tissues following abortion, ectopic or molar pregnancy

JA05.7.title: Other venous complications following abortion, ectopic or molar pregnancy

JA20.title: Pre-existing hypertension complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JA20.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females, caused by previously diagnosed maternal hypertension. This condition is characterised by any complication during pregnancy, childbirth, and the puerperium as a result of a blood pressure reading above 140/90 mmHg prior to the 20th week of pregnancy, or persisting longer than 12 weeks postpartum. Confirmation is by sphygmomanometer.

JA20.0.title: Pre-existing essential hypertension complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JA20.0.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females, caused by previously diagnosed, or diagnosed within the first 20 weeks, hypertension. This condition is characterised by blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg or greater, leading to a complication during pregnancy, childbirth, and the puerperium. Confirmation is by sphygmomanometer.

JA20.1.title: Pre-existing hypertensive heart disease complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JA20.1.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females, caused by previously diagnosed, or diagnosed within the first 20 weeks, hypertension and associated heart disease. This condition is characterised by blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg or greater, leading to a complication during pregnancy, childbirth, and the puerperium. Confirmation is by sphygmomanometer.

JA20.2.title: Pre-existing hypertensive renal disease complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JA20.2.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females, caused by previously diagnosed, or diagnosed within the first 20 weeks, hypertension and associated renal disease. This condition is characterised by blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg or greater, leading to a complication during pregnancy, childbirth, and the puerperium. Confirmation is by sphygmomanometer.

JA20.3.title: Pre-existing hypertensive heart and renal disease complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JA20.3.definition: Blood pressure of 140 mm Hg or greater systolic and/or 90 mm Hg or greater diastolic diagnosed preconception or in the first 20 weeks of pregnancy with associated heart and renal disease

JA20.4.title: Pre-existing secondary hypertension complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JA20.4.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females, caused by renal disease, endocrine disorders, or tumours. This condition is characterised by blood pressure greater than 140/90 mmHg prior to the 20th week of pregnancy, or persisting longer than 12 weeks postpartum, leading to a complication during pregnancy, childbirth, and the puerperium. Confirmation is by sphygmomanometer.

JA21.title: Pre-eclampsia superimposed on chronic hypertension
JA21.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females over 20 weeks gestation. This condition is characterised by systolic blood pressure greater than 140mmHg and diastolic greater or equal to 90mmHg on two occasions 4 hours apart in the presence of either proteinuria or other new onset maternal organ dysfunction characterised by one thrombocytopenia, elevated serum creatinine or liver transaminases, or neurological conditions or fetal growth restriction in a female diagnosed with pre-existing hypertension.

JA22.title: Gestational oedema or proteinuria without hypertension
JA22.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females, characterised by excessive systemic fluid build-up and serum proteins in the urine, without an abnormally elevated blood pressure induced by pregnancy.

JA22.2.title: Gestational oedema with proteinuria without hypertension
JA22.2.definition: The accumulation of fluid and proteinuria due to the physiological alterations of pregnancy in the absence of hypertension

JA23.title: Gestational hypertension
JA23.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females, characterised by systolic blood pressure greater than 140mmHg and/or a diastolic blood pressure greater or equal to 90mmHg on two occasions, 4 hours or more apart. Can be newly diagnosed after 20 weeks gestation or before 1 week postpartum. Confirmation is by measurement of blood pressure, liver and kidney functions test, and urine test.

JA24.title: Pre-eclampsia
JA24.definition: This condition is characterised by systolic blood pressure greater than 140 mmHg and/or diastolic greater or equal to 90 mmHg on two occasions 4 hours or more apart in the presence of either proteinuria or other new onset maternal organ dysfunction characterised by one thrombocytopenia, elevated serum creatinine or liver transaminases, or neurological conditions or fetal growth restriction.

JA24.0.title: Mild to moderate pre-eclampsia
JA24.0.definition: This condition is characterised by systolic blood pressure greater than 140 mmHg and/or diastolic greater or equal to 90 mmHg on two occasions 4 hours or more apart in the presence of either proteinuria or other new onset maternal organ dysfunction characterised by one thrombocytopenia, elevated serum creatinine or liver transaminases, or neurological conditions or fetal growth restriction.

JA24.1.title: Severe pre-eclampsia
JA24.1.definition: This condition is characterised by systolic blood pressure greater than 160 mmHg and/or diastolic greater or equal to 110 mmHg on two occasions 4 hours or more apart in the presence of either proteinuria or other new onset maternal organ dysfunction characterised by one thrombocytopenia, elevated serum creatinine or liver transaminases, or neurological conditions or fetal growth restriction.

JA24.2.title: HELLP syndrome
JA24.2.definition: Severe preeclampsia associated with haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, or low platelets

JA25.title: Eclampsia
JA25.definition: Any condition affecting pregnant females, characterised by seizure or convulsions newly arising in pregnancy. The condition is often associated with pregnancy-induced hypertension, convulsions, seizure, anxiety, epigastric pain, severe headache, blurred vision, proteinuria, and oedema that may occur during pregnancy, labour, or the puerperium.

JA25.0.title: Eclampsia in pregnancy
JA25.0.definition: This condition is characterised by seizure or convulsions newly arising in pregnancy. The condition is often associated with pregnancy-induced hypertension, convulsions, seizure, anxiety, epigastric pain, severe headache, blurred vision, proteinuria, and oedema that occurs during pregnancy.

JA25.1.title: Eclampsia in labour
JA25.1.definition: This condition is characterised by seizure or convulsions newly arising in pregnancy. The condition is often associated with pregnancy-induced hypertension, convulsions, seizure, anxiety, epigastric pain, severe headache, blurred vision, proteinuria, and oedema that occurs during labour.

JA25.2.title: Eclampsia in the puerperium
JA25.2.definition: This condition is characterised by seizure or convulsions newly arising in pregnancy. The condition is often associated with pregnancy-induced hypertension, convulsions, seizure, anxiety, epigastric pain, severe headache, blurred vision, proteinuria, and oedema that occurs during the puerperium.

JA25.3.title: Eclampsia, time period unspecified
JA25.3.definition: Onset of convulsions in a woman with pre-eclampsia not attributable to other causes without a specific onset time.

JA40.0.title: Threatened abortion
JA40.0.definition: A bloody vaginal discharge of bleeding appears through a closed cervical os during the first half of pregnancy.

JA42.0.title: Intrapartum haemorrhage with coagulation defect
JA42.0.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females, excluding those caused by abruptio placentae and placenta praevia. This condition is characterised by excessive loss of blood with difficulties in blood clotting factors, after 20 weeks gestation until labour and delivery.

JA42.1.title: Intrapartum haemorrhage resulting from obstructed labour with uterine rupture

JA42.2.title: Intrapartum haemorrhage resulting from obstructed labour without mention of uterine rupture
JA42.2.definition: Labour and delivery complicated by intrapartum haemorrhage from obstructed labour due to not otherwise specified causes or without mention of uterine rupture

JA43.0.title: Third-stage haemorrhage
JA43.0.definition: A condition characterised by excessive loss of blood during the third stage of labour for a vaginal delivery. This condition is caused by uterine atony, trauma, retained placenta, or coagulopathy.

JA43.1.title: Other immediate postpartum haemorrhage
JA43.1.definition: A condition characterised by excessive loss of blood within the first 24 hours after the completion of the third stage of labour for a vaginal delivery (more than 500 millilitres), or after a caesarean section (more than 1000 millilitres). This condition is caused by uterine atony, trauma, retained placenta, or coagulopathy.

JA43.2.title: Delayed or secondary postpartum haemorrhage
JA43.2.definition: A condition characterised by excessive loss of blood between 24 hours and 12 weeks after delivery. This condition is caused by uterine atony, trauma, retained placenta, or coagulopathy.

JA43.3.title: Postpartum coagulation defects
JA43.3.definition: A condition characterised by excessive loss of blood following a vaginal or caesarean section delivery. This condition is caused by coagulation defects during the postpartum period.

JA43.4.title: Postpartum haemorrhage following obstructed labour with uterine rupture

JA43.5.title: Postpartum haemorrhage following obstructed labour without mention of uterine rupture

JA60.0.title: Mild hyperemesis gravidarum
JA60.0.definition: Vomiting occurring during pregnancy responsive to dietary modification and antiemetic treatment

JA60.1.title: Hyperemesis gravidarum with metabolic disturbance
JA60.1.definition: Vomiting in pregnancy, not responsive to dietary modification and antiemetic treatment and associated with electrolyte disturbances and acid-base imbalance

JA60.2.title: Late vomiting of pregnancy
JA60.2.definition: Vomiting occurring after 22 completed weeks of gestation.

JA61.0.title: Varicose veins of lower extremity in pregnancy

JA61.4.title: Haemorrhoids in pregnancy
JA61.4.definition: A condition affecting females during pregnancy, caused by an increase in intra-abdominal pressure and hormonal changes during pregnancy. This condition is characterised by enlarged and varicosed haemorrhoidal veins in the anus and lower rectum. This condition may also present with itching, burning, painful swellings at the anus, dyschezia or rectal bleeding with bowel movements. Confirmation is by digital or visual examination with an anoscope, proctoscope, or sigmoidoscope of the anal canal and rectum to determine the presence of haemorrhoids.

JA62.title: Infections of genitourinary tract in pregnancy

JA62.3.title: Infections of other parts of urinary tract in pregnancy
JA62.3.definition: Infections of urinary tract other than kidney, bladder and urethra occurring during pregnancy

JA62.4.title: Infections of the genital tract in pregnancy

JA63.title: Diabetes mellitus in pregnancy
JA63.definition: A condition caused by dysfunctional maternal insulin receptors. This condition is characterised by glucose intolerance with onset or first recognition during pregnancy, with at least one of the following criteria met: fasting plasma glucose greater than or equal to 7.0 millimoles per litre (126 mg/dL); 2-hour plasma glucose greater than or equal to 11.1 millimoles per litre (200 mg/dL) following a 75 gram oral glucose load; random plasma glucose greater than or equal to 11.1 millimoles per litre (200 mg/dL). Confirmation is by an oral glucose tolerance test.

JA63.0.title: Pre-existing type 1 diabetes mellitus in pregnancy

JA63.1.title: Pre-existing type 2 diabetes mellitus in pregnancy

JA63.2.title: Diabetes mellitus arising in pregnancy
JA63.2.definition: Diabetes mellitus arising or diagnosed in pregnancy (Gestational diabetes mellitus) per WHO criteria or other national criteria. Gestational diabetes mellitus is defined as any degree of glucose intolerance with onset or first recognition during pregnancy. The definition applies regardless of whether insulin or only diet modification is used for treatment or whether the condition persists after pregnancy.

JA64.title: Malnutrition in pregnancy
JA64.definition: A condition caused by ingestion of a diet in which the nutrients are lacking or are in excess.

JA65.title: Maternal care for other conditions predominantly related to pregnancy
JA65.definition: Any reason for encounter to assess (or care for) a mother for other conditions predominantly related to pregnancy.

JA65.0.title: Liver disorders in pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JA65.0.definition: Any disorder affecting females, characterised by pathological changes to the liver that occur during pregnancy, childbirth, and the puerperium.

JA65.1.title: Pregnancy dermatoses
JA65.1.definition: A group of skin disorders which are specific to pregnancy.

JA65.10.title: Gestational pemphigoid
JA65.10.definition: Gestational pemphigoid (pemphigoid gestationis) is an autoimmune skin disease characterised by pruritic plaques and blister formation on the skin in association with pregnancy or the trophoblastic tumours, hydatiform mole and choriocarcinoma. The exact causes of the disease are unknown but the disease is mediated by auto-antibodies to the hemidesmosome component BP180/BPAg2/collagen XVII. The maternal antibodies may cause short lived disease in the neonate, neonatal pemphigoid gestationis. This disease is not an infection with herpes virus despite its old name, herpes gestationis.

JA65.11.title: Pruritus of pregnancy
JA65.11.definition: Pruritus in pregnancy can usually be attributed to a specific cause such as cholestasis, a pregnancy-specific dermatosis such as pruritic urticarial papules and plaques of pregnancy, or to exacerbation of a preexisting inflammatory dermatosis such as atopic eczema. Not uncommonly, however, a specific cause cannot be identified.

JA65.12.title: Polymorphic eruption of pregnancy
JA65.12.definition: Polymorphic eruption of pregnancy is a dermatosis which occurs almost exclusively in primigravidae or women with multiple pregnancy. It is associated with above average weight gain in pregnancy and it is thought that distension of abdominal skin is important in the pathogenesis: the precise mechanism is not understood. The eruption characteristically first appears in the third trimester of pregnancy as intensely itchy erythematous urticarial papules and plaques in and around the abdominal striae distensae. In some women it may then become more generalised. Onset is sometimes delayed until the immediate postpartum period. It does not usually recur in subsequent pregnancies.

JA65.2.title: Excessive weight gain in pregnancy
JA65.2.definition: Any reason for encounter to assess (or care for) a mother for excessive weight gain during pregnancy.

JA65.3.title: Low weight gain in pregnancy
JA65.3.definition: Any reason for encounter to assess (or care for) a mother for low weight gain during pregnancy.

JA65.4.title: Pregnancy care of habitual aborter
JA65.4.definition: Any reason for encounter to assess (or care for) a mother who has a history of habitual aborting.

JA65.5.title: Retained intrauterine contraceptive device in pregnancy
JA65.5.definition: Any reason for encounter to assess (or care for) a mother with a retained intrauterine contraceptive device during pregnancy.

JA65.6.title: Maternal hypotension syndrome
JA65.6.definition: Any reason for encounter to assess a mother for low blood pressure during pregnancy.

JA65.7.title: Subluxation of symphysis pubis in pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JA65.7.definition: Any reason for encounter to assess (or care for) a mother for subluxation of pubis symphysis during pregnancy.

JA66.title: Clinical findings on antenatal screening of mother
JA66.definition: Any sign characterised by an abnormality detected during an antenatal screening of the mother.

JA66.0.title: Abnormal haematological finding on antenatal screening of mother
JA66.0.definition: A sign characterised by an abnormality detected by haematology during an antenatal screening of the mother.

JA66.1.title: Abnormal biochemical finding on antenatal screening of mother
JA66.1.definition: A sign characterised by an abnormality detected by biochemistry during an antenatal screening of the mother.

JA66.2.title: Abnormal cytological finding on antenatal screening of mother
JA66.2.definition: A sign characterised by an abnormality detected by cytology during an antenatal screening of the mother.

JA66.3.title: Abnormal ultrasonic finding on antenatal screening of mother
JA66.3.definition: A sign characterised by an abnormality detected by ultrasound during an antenatal screening of the mother.

JA66.4.title: Abnormal radiological finding on antenatal screening of mother
JA66.4.definition: A sign characterised by an abnormality detected by radiology during an antenatal screening of the mother.

JA66.5.title: Abnormal chromosomal or genetic finding on antenatal screening of mother
JA66.5.definition: A sign characterised by a chromosomal or genetic abnormality detected during an antenatal screening of the mother.

JA67.0.title: Pulmonary complications of anaesthesia during pregnancy

JA67.1.title: Cardiac complications of anaesthesia during pregnancy

JA67.2.title: Central nervous system complications of anaesthesia during pregnancy

JA67.3.title: Toxic reaction to local anaesthesia during pregnancy
JA67.3.definition: A condition affecting females during pregnancy, caused by the properties or the concentration of the anaesthetic agent, or patient factors. This condition is characterised by a local or systemic toxic reaction leading to malfunctioning or failure of the neurovascular, central nervous, respiratory or cardiovascular systems with onset between 30 seconds and 60 minutes after administration of an anaesthetic.

JA67.4.title: Spinal or epidural anaesthesia-induced headache during pregnancy
JA67.4.definition: A condition affecting females during pregnancy, caused by the administration of spinal and epidural anaesthesia. This condition is characterised by cephalgia during pregnancy.

JA67.5.title: Failed or difficult intubation during pregnancy
JA67.5.definition: A condition affecting females during pregnancy, caused by physiological, pathophysiological, or psychological factors that aggravate the tissues necessary to secure the tube. This condition is characterised by a difficulty or inability to insert a tube into an external or internal orifice of the body during pregnancy.

JA67.6.title: Awareness under general anaesthesia during pregnancy

JA80.title: Maternal care related to multiple gestation

JA81.title: Maternal care related to complications specific to multiple gestation

JA81.1.title: Continuing pregnancy after abortion of one fetus or more

JA81.2.title: Continuing pregnancy after intrauterine death of one fetus or more

JA81.3.title: Loss of pregnancy after abortion or intrauterine death of one fetus or more

JA82.title: Maternal care for malpresentation of fetus
JA82.definition: Care provided for the pregnant female for incorrect position or orientation of the fetus at near term or during labour, determined by its relation to the spine of the mother and the birth canal.

JA82.2.title: Maternal care for transverse or oblique lie

JA82.3.title: Maternal care for face, brow or chin presentation

JA82.4.title: Maternal care for high head at term

JA82.5.title: Maternal care for multiple gestation with malpresentation of one fetus or more

JA83.title: Maternal care for disproportion
JA83.definition: A condition characterised by the provision of health interventions to the mother due to the situation in which the head or body of the fetus is too large to fit through the pelvis of the mother.

JA83.0.title: Maternal care for disproportion due to deformity of maternal pelvic bones

JA83.1.title: Maternal care for disproportion due to generally contracted pelvis

JA83.2.title: Maternal care for disproportion due to inlet contraction of pelvis

JA83.3.title: Maternal care for disproportion due to outlet contraction of pelvis

JA83.4.title: Maternal care for disproportion of mixed maternal and fetal origin

JA83.5.title: Maternal care for disproportion due to unusually large fetus

JA83.6.title: Maternal care for disproportion due to hydrocephalic fetus

JA84.title: Maternal care for abnormality of pelvic organs
JA84.definition: A condition characterised by the provision of health interventions to the mother due to some abnormality that is either suspected or known to be present in one or more of her pelvic organs.

JA84.0.title: Maternal care for congenital malformation of uterus
JA84.0.definition: Care provided for the pregnant female necessary due to malformation of the pregnant female's uterus present at or before the time of birth.

JA84.1.title: Maternal care for tumour of corpus uteri
JA84.1.definition: Care provided for the pregnant female necessary due to the presence of a uterine tumour at the time of pregnancy.

JA84.2.title: Maternal care due to uterine scar from previous surgery

JA84.4.title: Maternal care for abnormality of vagina
JA84.4.definition: Care provided for the pregnant female necessary due to some abnormality of the vagina.

JA84.5.title: Maternal care for abnormality of vulva or perineum

JA85.title: Maternal care for fetal abnormality or damage
JA85.definition: A condition characterised by the provision of health interventions to the mother due to some abnormality or damage that is either suspected or known to be present in the fetus.

JA85.0.title: Maternal care for central nervous system malformation in fetus

JA85.1.title: Maternal care for chromosomal abnormality in fetus

JA85.2.title: Maternal care for hereditary disease in fetus

JA85.3.title: Maternal care for damage to fetus from viral disease in mother

JA86.title: Maternal care for other fetal problems
JA86.definition: A condition characterised by the provision of health interventions to the mother due to any other issue that is either suspected or known to be present in the fetus.

JA86.0.title: Maternal care for red cell antibodies
JA86.0.definition: Maternal care for rhesus or other isoimmunization

JA86.2.title: Maternal care for signs of fetal hypoxia

JA86.4.title: Maternal care for fetal growth restriction

JA86.6.title: Maternal care for viable fetus in abdominal pregnancy

JA87.title: Maternal care related to polyhydramnios
JA87.definition: Excessive amniotic fluid normally diagnosed on ultrasound either subjectively using either single deepest vertical pocket of greater or equal to 8 cm and/or amniotic fluid index greater or equal to 24 cm.

JA88.title: Maternal care related to certain specified disorders of amniotic fluid or membranes

JA88.1.title: Infection of amniotic sac or membranes

JA89.title: Maternal care related to premature rupture of membranes
JA89.definition: Spontaneous rupture of fetal membranes before the onset of labour.

JA89.0.title: Premature rupture of membranes, onset of labour within 24 hours

JA89.1.title: Premature rupture of membranes, onset of labour after 24 hours

JA89.2.title: Premature rupture of membranes, labour delayed by therapy

JA8A.title: Maternal care related to placental disorders

JA8B.title: Maternal care related to placenta praevia or low lying placenta
JA8B.definition: A placenta that is implanted over or very near the internal cervical os.

JA8B.0.title: Placenta praevia specified as without haemorrhage

JA8C.title: Maternal care related to premature separation of placenta

JA8C.0.title: Premature separation of placenta with coagulation defect

JA8D.title: Maternal care related to false labour
JA8D.definition: Contractions suggestive of labour but which do not lead to cervical dilatation.

JA8D.0.title: False labour before 37 completed weeks of gestation

JA8D.1.title: False labour at or after 37 completed weeks of gestation

JA8E.title: Maternal care related to prolonged pregnancy
JA8E.definition: Pregnancy that has exceeded a duration of 42 weeks from the last menstrual period.

JB00.title: Preterm labour or delivery
JB00.definition: A condition characterised by the onset of labour and delivery before 37 completed weeks. Assign an additional extension code, if desired, for Duration of pregnancy.

JB00.0.title: Preterm labour without delivery
JB00.0.definition: A condition characterised by the onset of labour before 37 completed weeks, without delivery.

JB00.1.title: Preterm spontaneous labour with preterm delivery
JB00.1.definition: A condition characterised by the spontaneous onset of labour and delivery before 37 completed weeks.

JB00.2.title: Preterm labour with term delivery
JB00.2.definition: A condition characterised by the spontaneous onset of labour before 37 completed weeks followed by a delivery after 39 weeks.

JB00.3.title: Preterm delivery following iatrogenic induction of labour or caesarean section

JB01.title: Failed induction of labour
JB01.definition: A condition characterised by a failed attempt to stimulate contractions before the spontaneous onset of labour. This condition may occur with or without ruptured membranes.

JB01.0.title: Failed medical induction of labour
JB01.0.definition: A condition characterised by a failed attempt to stimulate contractions pharmacologically before the spontaneous onset of labour. This condition may occur with or without ruptured membranes.

JB01.1.title: Failed instrumental induction of labour
JB01.1.definition: A condition characterised by a failed attempt to instrumentally stimulate contractions before the spontaneous onset of labour. This condition may occur with or without ruptured membranes.

JB02.title: Abnormalities of forces of labour
JB02.definition: Any condition affecting pregnant females, characterised by an anomaly or dysfunction to the tissues or processes associated with the natural progression of labour. These conditions may lead to further complications during labour and childbirth.

JB02.0.title: Primary uterine inertia
JB02.0.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females characterised by insufficiently strong or inappropriately coordinated rhythmic activity of the myometrium during labour to efface and dilate the cervix.

JB02.1.title: Secondary uterine inertia
JB02.1.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females that is idiopathic. This condition is characterised by vigorous contractions that decrease in vigour due to exhaustion or dehydration of the individual. This condition leads to lack of labour progress.

JB02.2.title: Other uterine inertia
JB02.2.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females that is idiopathic. This condition is characterised by the absence of effective uterine contractions during labour and abnormal relaxation of the uterus during labour. This condition leads to lack of labour progress or uterine haemorrhage.

JB02.3.title: Precipitate labour
JB02.3.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females that is idiopathic. This condition is characterised by rapid labour and the lack of time for standard obstetric preparations or procedures leading to the delivery of the newborn. This condition leads to vaginal bleeding, frequent strong contractions, feelings of defecation, crowning of the fetus head at the vaginal introitus, or bulging of the amniotic sac.

JB02.4.title: Hypertonic, incoordinate, or prolonged uterine contractions
JB02.4.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females that is idiopathic. This condition is characterised by uterine dysfunction leading to hypertonic, uncoordinated, and prolonged rhythmic activity of the myometrium during labour.

JB03.title: Long labour
JB03.definition: Any condition characterised by a longer than average parturition between the initiation of regular, rhythmic, and painful contractions and cervical dilation, to the delivery of the placenta.

JB03.0.title: Prolonged first stage of labour
JB03.0.definition: The first stage of labour where cervical dilatation progresses less than 1 centimetre per hour for a minimum of 4 hours. Protracted descent is less than 1 centimetre per hour for nulliparas and less than 2 centimetre per hour for multiparas.

JB03.1.title: Prolonged second stage of labour
JB03.1.definition: The fetus has not been delivered after the cervix has become fully dilated within 2 hours for a primipara, or 1 hour for a multipara. Presence of regional anaesthesia will add 1 hour.

JB03.2.title: Delayed delivery of successive neonates
JB03.2.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females, characterised by the delayed spontaneous or caesarean section delivery of the successive neonates in a multiple delivery.

JB04.title: Obstructed labour due to malposition or malpresentation of fetus
JB04.definition: A condition affecting pregnant females, caused by the abnormal position of fetal head or the abnormal presentation of the fetus away from the fetal head in vertex.

JB04.0.title: Obstructed labour due to incomplete rotation of fetal head

JB04.1.title: Obstructed labour due to breech presentation

JB04.2.title: Obstructed labour due to face presentation

JB04.3.title: Obstructed labour due to brow presentation

JB04.4.title: Obstructed labour due to shoulder presentation

JB04.5.title: Obstructed labour due to compound presentation

JB05.title: Obstructed labour due to maternal pelvic abnormality
JB05.definition: Obstructed labour means that, in spite of strong contractions of the uterus, the fetus cannot descend through the pelvis because there is an insurmountable barrier preventing its descent. Obstruction usually occurs at the pelvic brim, but occasionally it may occur in the cavity or at the outlet of the pelvis. Complications resulting from obstructed labour can be avoided if a woman in obstructed labour is identified early and appropriate action is taken.

JB05.0.title: Obstructed labour due to deformed pelvis

JB05.1.title: Obstructed labour due to generally contracted pelvis

JB05.2.title: Obstructed labour due to pelvic inlet contraction

JB05.3.title: Obstructed labour due to pelvic outlet or mid-cavity contraction

JB05.4.title: Obstructed labour due to foetopelvic disproportion, unspecified

JB05.5.title: Obstructed labour due to abnormality of maternal pelvic organs

JB06.title: Obstructed labour due to other causes
JB06.definition: Any other condition characterised by the inability of the presenting part of the fetus to progress into the birth canal for any reason.

JB06.0.title: Obstructed labour due to shoulder dystocia

JB06.1.title: Obstructed labour due to locked twins

JB06.2.title: Obstructed labour due to unusually large fetus

JB06.3.title: Obstructed labour due to other abnormalities of fetus

JB07.title: Labour or delivery complicated by fetal distress

JB07.0.title: Labour or delivery complicated by fetal heart rate anomaly
JB07.0.definition: A condition characterised by an abnormal fetal heart rate. This condition leads to further difficulties and complications during labour and delivery. Confirmation is by Doppler ultrasound.

JB07.1.title: Labour or delivery complicated by meconium in amniotic fluid
JB07.1.definition: A condition characterised by complications during labour and delivery that is caused by meconium in amniotic fluid.

JB07.2.title: Labour or delivery complicated by biochemical evidence of fetal stress
JB07.2.definition: A condition characterised by complications during labour and delivery that is caused by biochemical evidence of fetal distress. Confirmation is by a fetal blood sample from a scalp prick through the open cervix during labour.

JB08.title: Labour or delivery complicated by umbilical cord complications

JB08.0.title: Labour or delivery complicated by prolapse of cord
JB08.0.definition: A condition characterised by complications during labour and delivery that is caused by umbilical cord prolapse.

JB08.1.title: Labour or delivery complicated by cord around neck, with compression
JB08.1.definition: A condition characterised by complications during labour and delivery that is caused by wrapping of the umbilical cord around the neck of the fetus, with compression.

JB08.2.title: Labour or delivery complicated by short cord
JB08.2.definition: A condition characterised by complications during labour and delivery that is caused by a short umbilical cord.

JB08.3.title: Labour or delivery complicated by vasa praevia
JB08.3.definition: A condition characterised by complications during labour and delivery that is caused when the umbilical vessels traverse the membranes of the internal cervical os.

JB08.4.title: Labour or delivery complicated by vascular lesion of cord
JB08.4.definition: A condition characterised by complications during labour and delivery that is caused by vascular lesion of the umbilical cord.

JB08.5.title: Labour or delivery complicated by other cord entanglement, with compression

JB09.title: Perineal laceration during delivery
JB09.definition: An injury characterised by a laceration to the maternal perineum during delivery.

JB09.0.title: First degree perineal laceration during delivery
JB09.0.definition: Perineal lacerations involving the fourchette, perineal skin, and vaginal mucous membrane but not the underlying fascia and muscle.

JB09.1.title: Second degree perineal laceration during delivery
JB09.1.definition: Perineal lacerations involve, in addition, the fascia and muscles of the perineal body but not the anal sphincter.

JB09.2.title: Third degree perineal laceration during delivery
JB09.2.definition: Perineal lacerations extending farther to involve the anal sphincter.

JB09.3.title: Fourth degree perineal laceration during delivery
JB09.3.definition: Perineal lacerations extending through the rectum's mucosa to expose its lumen.

JB0A.title: Certain specified obstetric trauma
JB0A.definition: Any injury characterised by maternal trauma. These injuries are caused by or subsequent to the process of (or any intervention related to) pregnancy, or labour and delivery.

JB0A.0.title: Rupture of uterus before onset of labour
JB0A.0.definition: An injury characterised by rupture of the myometrial wall of the uterus before the onset of labour. This injury is caused by pregnancy. This injury presents with abdominal pain, haemorrhage, or hypovolemic shock in the mother, or late decelerations, reduced variability, tachycardia, or bradycardia in the fetus.

JB0A.1.title: Rupture of uterus during labour
JB0A.1.definition: An injury characterised by rupture of the myometrial wall of the uterus during labour. This injury is caused by or subsequent to the process of (or any intervention related to) pregnancy, or labour and delivery. This injury presents with abdominal pain, haemorrhage, or hypovolemic shock in the mother, or late decelerations, reduced variability, tachycardia, or bradycardia in the fetus.

JB0A.2.title: Postpartum inversion of uterus
JB0A.2.definition: An injury characterised by uterine inversion and prolapse through the dilated cervix that occurs after the delivery of a neonate. This condition is caused by or subsequent to labour and delivery, commonly as a result of excessive fundal pressure or cord traction. This condition presents with postpartum haemorrhage.

JB0A.3.title: Obstetric laceration of cervix
JB0A.3.definition: An injury characterised by a laceration to the cervix. This injury is caused by or subsequent to the process of (or any intervention related to) pregnancy, or labour and delivery.

JB0A.4.title: Obstetric high vaginal laceration
JB0A.4.definition: An injury characterised by a laceration in the upper third area of the vagina. This injury is caused by or subsequent to the process of (or any intervention related to) pregnancy, or labour and delivery.

JB0A.6.title: Other obstetric injury to pelvic organs
JB0A.6.definition: Any injury characterised by damage to the maternal pelvic organs. These injuries are caused by or subsequent to the process of (or any intervention related to) pregnancy, or labour and delivery.

JB0A.7.title: Obstetric damage to pelvic joints or ligaments
JB0A.7.definition: An injury characterised by damage to the pelvic joints and ligaments. This injury is caused by or subsequent to the process of (or any intervention related to) pregnancy, or labour and delivery.

JB0A.8.title: Obstetric haematoma of pelvis
JB0A.8.definition: An injury characterised by a collection of extravasated blood trapped in the pelvic tissues. This injury is caused by or subsequent to the process of (or any intervention related to) pregnancy, or labour and delivery. This condition may also present with bruising or blood clots in the pelvic area.

JB0B.title: Retained placenta or membranes, without haemorrhage
JB0B.definition: A condition characterised by a placenta or membranes that have not been expelled from the uterus during the third stage of labour and up to 30 minutes following delivery, and without haemorrhage. This condition is caused by uterine atony, a trapped placenta, or a placenta accreta. This condition may lead to primary postpartum haemorrhage or infection.

JB0B.0.title: Retained placenta without haemorrhage
JB0B.0.definition: A condition characterised by a placenta that has not been expelled from the uterus during the third stage of labour and up to 30 minutes following delivery, and without haemorrhage. This condition is caused by uterine atony, a trapped placenta, or a placenta accreta. This condition may lead to primary postpartum haemorrhage or infection.

JB0B.1.title: Retained portions of placenta or membranes, without haemorrhage
JB0B.1.definition: A condition characterised by portions of a placenta and membranes that have not been expelled from the uterus during the third stage of labour and up to 30 minutes following delivery, and without haemorrhage. This condition is caused by uterine atony, a trapped placenta, or a placenta accreta. This condition may lead to primary postpartum haemorrhage or infection.

JB0C.title: Complications of anaesthesia during labour or delivery
JB0C.definition: Any complication caused by or subsequent to any anaesthetic intervention used during labour and delivery.

JB0C.0.title: Aspiration pneumonitis due to anaesthesia during labour or delivery
JB0C.0.definition: Massive gastric inhalation causing pulmonary insufficiency from aspiration pneumonitis due to anaesthesia during labour and delivery.

JB0C.1.title: Other pulmonary complications of anaesthesia during labour or delivery

JB0C.2.title: Cardiac complications of anaesthesia during labour or delivery

JB0C.3.title: Central nervous system complications of anaesthesia during labour or delivery

JB0C.4.title: Toxic reaction to local anaesthesia during labour or delivery

JB0C.5.title: Spinal or epidural anaesthesia-induced headache during labour or delivery

JB0C.6.title: Other complications of spinal or epidural anaesthesia during labour or delivery

JB0C.7.title: Failed or difficult intubation during labour or delivery

JB0C.70.title: Failed intubation during labour or delivery

JB0C.71.title: Difficult intubation during labour or delivery

JB0C.8.title: Awareness under general anaesthesia during labour or delivery

JB0D.title: Certain specified complications of labour or delivery, not elsewhere classified

JB0D.0.title: Maternal distress during labour or delivery
JB0D.0.definition: A condition characterised by maternal anxiety, depression, or stress during labour and delivery.

JB0D.1.title: Shock during or following labour or delivery
JB0D.1.definition: A syndrome characterised by systemic cellular hypoxia and organ dysfunction as a result of hypoperfusion following labour and delivery. This syndrome is caused by haemorrhage, vomiting, diarrhoea, inadequate fluid intake, or a systemic inflammatory response to bacteria, endotoxins, or exotoxins.

JB0D.2.title: Pyrexia during labour, not elsewhere classified
JB0D.2.definition: A complication characterised by maternal fever during labour, and not elsewhere classified.

JB0D.3.title: Other complications of obstetric surgery or procedures
JB0D.3.definition: Any complication caused by or subsequent to obstetric surgery and procedures, and not elsewhere classified.

JB0D.4.title: Delayed delivery after artificial rupture of membranes
JB0D.4.definition: A complication characterised by a delayed neonatal delivery after the artificial rupture of the membranes.

JB0D.5.title: Delayed delivery after spontaneous or unspecified rupture of membranes
JB0D.5.definition: A complication characterised by a delayed neonatal delivery after the spontaneous or unspecified rupture of the membranes.

JB0D.6.title: Vaginal delivery following previous caesarean section

JB0D.7.title: Failed application of vacuum extractor or forceps, unspecified

JB20.title: Single spontaneous delivery
JB20.definition: A condition caused by the development of a fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by spontaneous parturition of a neonate from the uterus.

JB20.0.title: Single spontaneous vertex delivery
JB20.0.definition: A condition caused by the development of a fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by spontaneous parturition of a neonate in vertex position from the uterus.

JB20.1.title: Single spontaneous breech delivery
JB20.1.definition: A condition caused by the development of a fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by spontaneous parturition of a neonate in breech position from the uterus.

JB21.title: Single delivery by forceps or vacuum extractor
JB21.definition: A condition caused by the development of a fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by parturition of a neonate from the uterus using forceps and vacuum extractor to assist the delivery.

JB22.title: Single delivery by caesarean section
JB22.definition: A condition caused by the development of a fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by parturition of a single neonate from the uterus by caesarean section.

JB22.2.title: Single delivery by caesarean hysterectomy
JB22.2.definition: A condition caused by the development of a fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by parturition of a neonate from the uterus by caesarean section followed by removal of the uterus.

JB23.0.title: Breech extraction
JB23.0.definition: A condition caused by the development of a fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by parturition of a neonate in breech position from the uterus using breech extraction interventions or techniques to assist the delivery.

JB23.1.title: Other assisted breech delivery
JB23.1.definition: A condition caused by the development of a fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by parturition of a neonate in breech position from the uterus using other interventions or techniques to assist the delivery.

JB23.2.title: Other manipulation-assisted delivery
JB23.2.definition: A condition caused by the development of a fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by parturition of a neonate from the uterus using other manipulation-assisted interventions or techniques to assist the delivery.

JB23.3.title: Delivery of viable fetus in abdominal pregnancy
JB23.3.definition: A condition caused by the development of a viable fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by parturition of a viable neonate from the abdominal cavity, at the culmination of an abdominal pregnancy.

JB23.4.title: Destructive operation for delivery
JB23.4.definition: A condition caused by the development of a fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by parturition of a neonate using destructive operation interventions or techniques to assist the delivery.

JB24.title: Multiple delivery
JB24.definition: A condition caused by the development of more than one fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by parturition of more than one neonate from the uterus either spontaneously, assisted, or by caesarean section.

JB24.0.title: Multiple delivery, all spontaneous
JB24.0.definition: A condition caused by the development of more than one fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by parturition of more than one neonate spontaneously from the uterus.

JB24.1.title: Multiple delivery, all by forceps or vacuum extractor
JB24.1.definition: A condition caused by the development of more than one fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by parturition of more than one neonate from the uterus using forceps and vacuum extractor.

JB24.2.title: Multiple delivery, all by caesarean section
JB24.2.definition: A condition caused by the development of more than one fetus to the culmination of the pregnancy period. This condition is characterised by parturition of more than one neonate from the uterus by caesarean section.

JB24.3.title: Multiple delivery by combination of methods with caesarean

JB40.2.title: Other infection of genital tract following delivery

JB40.4.title: Pyrexia of unknown origin following delivery

JB41.3.title: Cerebral venous thrombosis in the puerperium

JB42.title: Obstetric embolism
JB42.definition: A condition characterised by the lodging of a blood clot, a fat globule or a gas bubble (embolus) in the bloodstream, which can cause a blockage associated with the physiological and other changes that occur during the period of time from conception to delivery (pregnancy), during labour and delivery (childbirth) or during the approximately six weeks after delivery during which the uterus returns to the original size (puerperium).

JB42.0.title: Obstetric air embolism
JB42.0.definition: A condition characterised by the lodging of a gas bubble (air embolus) in the bloodstream, which can cause a blockage associated with the physiological and other changes that occur during the period of time from conception to delivery (pregnancy), during labour and delivery (childbirth) or during the approximately six weeks after delivery during which the uterus returns to the original size (puerperium).

JB42.1.title: Amniotic fluid embolism
JB42.1.definition: Amniotic fluid embolism is a rare obstetric emergency in which it is postulated that amniotic fluid, fetal cells, hair, or other debris enter the maternal circulation, causing cardiorespiratory collapse.

JB42.2.title: Obstetric blood-clot embolism
JB42.2.definition: A condition characterised by the lodging of a blood clot (a specific type of embolus known as a thrombus) in the bloodstream, which can cause a blockage associated with the physiological and other changes that occur during the period of time from conception to delivery (pregnancy), during labour and delivery (childbirth) or during the approximately six weeks after delivery during which the uterus returns to the original size (puerperium).

JB43.title: Complications of anaesthesia during the puerperium

JB43.0.title: Pulmonary complications of anaesthesia during the puerperium

JB43.1.title: Cardiac complications of anaesthesia during the puerperium

JB43.2.title: Central nervous system complications of anaesthesia during the puerperium

JB43.3.title: Spinal or epidural anaesthesia-induced headache during the puerperium

JB43.4.title: Other complications of spinal or epidural anaesthesia during the puerperium

JB43.5.title: Failed or difficult intubation during the puerperium

JB43.6.title: Awareness under general anaesthesia during the puerperium

JB44.title: Certain specified complications of the puerperium
JB44.definition: A group of conditions characterised as any adverse evolution (complication) which may arise during the approximately six weeks after delivery during which the uterus returns to the original size (puerperium) which are not classified elsewhere.

JB44.3.title: Cardiomyopathy in the puerperium
JB44.3.definition: A group of diseases in which the dominant feature is the involvement of the cardiac muscle itself occurring in puerperium, the period of 6-8 weeks after giving birth. Cardiomyopathies are classified according to their predominant pathophysiological features or their etiological/pathological factors.

JB44.5.title: Postpartum thyroiditis
JB44.5.definition: Postpartum thyroiditis (PPT) is the occurrence, in the postpartum period, of transient hyperthyroidism and/or transient hypothyroidism, with most women returning to the euthyroid state by 1 year postpartum.

JB45.title: Infections of breast associated with childbirth

JB45.0.title: Abscess of breast associated with childbirth

JB46.title: Certain specified disorders of breast or lactation associated with childbirth

JB46.0.title: Retracted nipple associated with childbirth
JB46.0.definition: A condition characterised as the abnormal inversion of a nipple that does not return to normal position even when stimulated that has occurred in association with childbirth.

JB46.2.title: Other or unspecified disorders of breast associated with childbirth

JB46.6.title: Galactorrhoea
JB46.6.definition: Excessive or inappropriate lactation in females or males, and not necessarily related to pregnancy. Galactorrhoea can occur either unilaterally or bilaterally, and be profuse or sparse. Its most common cause is hyperprolactinemia.

JB46.7.title: Other or unspecified disorders of lactation

JB60.title: Obstetric death of unspecified cause
JB60.definition: A condition characterised by maternal death during pregnancy or within 42 days following delivery. This death may be associated with physiological, obstetrical, or other changes or is provoked by interventions used during pregnancy, childbirth, or puerperium, but has no specified cause.

JB61.title: Death from any obstetric cause occurring more than 42 days but less than one year after delivery
JB61.definition: A condition characterised by maternal death between 43 days and one year following delivery. This death is caused by any physiological, obstetrical, or other changes or is provoked by interventions used during pregnancy, childbirth, or puerperium.

JB61.0.title: Death from direct obstetric cause occurring more than 42 days but less than one year after delivery
JB61.0.definition: Any condition directly resulting in death due to any cause associated with the physiological or other changes that occur during the period of time from conception to delivery (pregnancy), during labour and delivery (childbirth) or during the approximately six weeks after delivery during which the uterus returns to the original size (puerperium).

JB61.1.title: Death from indirect obstetric cause occurring more than 42 days but less than one year after delivery
JB61.1.definition: Any condition indirectly resulting in death via an intermediate cause due to any issue associated with the physiological or other changes that occur during the period of time from conception to delivery (pregnancy), during labour and delivery (childbirth) or during the approximately six weeks after delivery during which the uterus returns to the original size (puerperium).

JB62.title: Death from sequelae of obstetric causes
JB62.definition: A secondary condition of pregnant females, caused by and subsequent to any complications during pregnancy, childbirth, or puerperium. This condition is characterised by maternal death.

JB62.0.title: Death from sequelae of direct obstetric cause
JB62.0.definition: Any condition directly resulting in death due to a pathological condition resulting from any adverse evolution (complication) which may arise associated with the period of time from conception to delivery (pregnancy), during labour and delivery (childbirth) or during the approximately six weeks after delivery during which the uterus returns to the original size (puerperium).

JB62.1.title: Death from sequelae of indirect obstetric cause
JB62.1.definition: Any condition resulting in death via an intermediate cause due to a pathological condition resulting from any adverse evolution (complication) which may arise associated with the period of time from conception to delivery (pregnancy), during labour and delivery (childbirth) or during the approximately six weeks after delivery during which the uterus returns to the original size (puerperium).

JB63.title: Maternal infectious diseases classifiable elsewhere but complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JB63.definition: Maternal infectious and parasitic diseases classifiable elsewhere but complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium

JB63.0.title: Tuberculosis complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium

JB63.1.title: Syphilis complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JB63.1.definition: Syphilis complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium

JB63.2.title: Gonorrhoea complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium

JB63.3.title: Other infections with a predominantly sexual mode of transmission complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium

JB63.4.title: Viral hepatitis complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium

JB63.5.title: Other viral diseases complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium

JB63.6.title: Protozoal diseases complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium

JB63.60.title: Malaria complicating pregnancy, childbirth, or the puerperium

JB63.7.title: Human immunodeficiency disease complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium

JB64.title: Certain maternal diseases classifiable elsewhere but complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium

JB64.0.title: Anaemia complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JB64.0.definition: A condition of the circulatory system affecting pregnant females, characterised by a haemoglobin level below 11 grams per decilitre that complicates pregnancy, childbirth, or the puerperium.

JB64.1.title: Other diseases of the blood or blood-forming organs or certain disorders involving the immune mechanism complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JB64.1.definition: Any disease affecting pregnant females, characterised by pathological changes to the blood and blood-forming organs and pathological changes involving the immune mechanism that complicate pregnancy, childbirth, or the puerperium not classified elsewhere.

JB64.2.title: Endocrine, nutritional or metabolic diseases complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JB64.2.definition: Any disease affecting pregnant females, characterised by endocrine, nutrition, or metabolic manifestations that complicate pregnancy, childbirth, or the puerperium.

JB64.3.title: Diseases of the nervous system complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JB64.3.definition: Any disorder or disease of the nervous system affecting pregnant females leading to complications during pregnancy, childbirth, or puerperium.

JB64.4.title: Diseases of the circulatory system complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium

JB64.5.title: Diseases of the respiratory system complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium

JB64.6.title: Diseases of the digestive system complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium

JB64.7.title: Diseases of the skin complicating pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JB64.7.definition: Diseases of the skin or subcutaneous tissue not specifically related to pregnancy but which contribute to increased morbidity during pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium, for example genetic blistering disorders or lichen sclerosus.

JB65.title: Sequelae of complication of pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium
JB65.definition: A secondary condition that develops during the period of time from conception to delivery (pregnancy), during labour and delivery (childbirth) or during the six weeks following delivery (puerperium).

KA00.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal conditions that may be unrelated to present pregnancy
KA00.definition: A group of conditions characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to conditions associated with the mother which are unrelated to the present pregnancy.

KA00.0.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal hypertensive disorders
KA00.0.definition: Maternal hypertensive disorders (chronic hypertension, preeclampsia, eclampsia, preeclampsia superimposed on chronic hypertension, or gestational hypertension).

KA00.1.title: Fetus or newborn affected by gestational oedema or proteinuria without hypertension

KA00.2.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal renal or urinary tract diseases
KA00.2.definition: A group of conditions characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to conditions in the mother associated with the kidneys or urinary tract.

KA00.3.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal infectious diseases
KA00.3.definition: A condition affecting fetuses or newborns, that is (or suspected to be) caused by a maternal infection with a bacterial, viral, fungal, or parasitic source.

KA00.4.title: Fetus or newborn affected by periodontal disease in mother

KA00.5.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal respiratory diseases

KA00.6.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal nutritional disorders
KA00.6.definition: A group of conditions characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to conditions in the mother that are directly or indirectly associated with a lack of essential nutrients in the diet.

KA00.60.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal malnutrition

KA00.61.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal overweight or obesity

KA00.7.title: Fetus or newborn affected by abnormal maternal chemistry

KA00.8.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal injury
KA00.8.definition: A group of conditions characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to conditions in the mother resulting from physical damage or harm.

KA00.9.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal chemotherapy

KA00.A.title: Fetus or newborn affected by surgical procedure on mother
KA00.A.definition: A group of conditions characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to conditions in the mother resulting from surgical health intervention.

KA00.B.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal anaemia

KA01.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal complications of pregnancy
KA01.definition: Any other condition characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to any condition of the mother due to an adverse evolution (complication) which may arise associated with the time period from conception through childbirth.

KA01.0.title: Fetus or newborn affected by incompetence of cervix uteri
KA01.0.definition: Cervical incompetence refers to a weakness of the cervix and lower uterine segment, which can lead to recurrent second-trimester or early third-trimester loss of pregnancy due to an inability of the uterine cervix to retain a pregnancy until term. It is associated with a premature shortening of the cervix, dilatation, and opening of the cervical os during pregnancy. Ultrasound changes that suggest cervical incompetence include a cervical length < 1.5 cm, cervical width > 3 cm, and an expanded cervical canal > 8 mm.

KA01.1.title: Fetus or newborn affected by premature rupture of membranes
KA01.1.definition: Preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) refers to a patient who is at less than 37 weeks’ gestation and has presented with a rupture of membranes prior to the onset of labour. Complications include pre-term delivery, ascending infection, umbilical cord prolapse, oligohydramnios, placental abruption, retained placenta, postpartum haemorrhage, or rupture of the vasa praevia.

KA01.2.title: Fetus or newborn affected by oligohydramnios
KA01.2.definition: Oligohydramnios is defined as a decrease in the volume of amniotic fluid. It is diagnosed if the diameter of the largest amniotic fluid depot is < 2 cm, or if the amniotic fluid index (AFI) is < 5 cm.

KA01.3.title: Fetus or newborn affected by polyhydramnios
KA01.3.definition: Polyhydramnios is defined as an abnormally large volume of amniotic fluid within the uterus. An amount of 2 litres at term, any single pool >8cm or an amniotic fluid index (AFI) > 24 cm is considered to be polyhydramnios.

KA01.4.title: Fetus or newborn affected by ectopic pregnancy
KA01.4.definition: An ectopic pregnancy occurs when a pregnancy begins outside of the uterus. The most common site is within one of the fallopian tubes, although in rare cases, ectopic pregnancies can occur in the stomach region, cervix, or ovary. It is often caused by a condition that slows or blocks the movement of a fertilised egg through the fallopian tube to the uterus. Ectopic pregnancies cannot continue to term and the developing cells must be removed to prevent rupture of the ectopic area, which can lead to shock and danger the life of the mother.

KA01.5.title: Fetus or newborn affected by multiple pregnancy
KA01.5.definition: A condition characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to any condition associated with the presence of a multiple pregnancy.

KA01.6.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal death
KA01.6.definition: A condition characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to death of the mother.

KA01.7.title: Fetus or newborn affected by malpresentation before labour
KA01.7.definition: Malpresentations are all presentations of the fetus other than the vertex, and includes breech, transverse, shoulder, compound, face, and brow presentations. They may pose risks to the fetus and mother and may necessitate operative vaginal or caesarean delivery, or other interventions to accomplish delivery. Breech presentation, the most common malpresentation, results when the fetal buttocks, legs, feet, or a combination of these presents first into the maternal pelvis.

KA01.8.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal blood loss

KA02.title: Fetus or newborn affected by complications of placenta
KA02.definition: A group of conditions characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to an adverse evolution (complication) associated with the placenta, umbilical cord, or chorioamniotic membranes.

KA02.0.title: Fetus or newborn affected by placenta praevia
KA02.0.definition: Placenta praevia exists when the placenta lies wholly or in part in the lower segment of the uterus. Diagnosis has evolved from the clinical I-IV grading system, and is determined by ultrasonic imaging techniques relating the leading edge of the placenta to the cervical os.
