Grade I is a low lying placenta, Grade II is a placenta that meets the edge of the cervical os, Grade III is a placenta that partially covers the os, and Grade IV is a placenta that completely covers the os.

KA02.1.title: Fetus or newborn affected by placental oedema or large placenta
KA02.1.definition: A large placenta, also known as placentomegaly, is one that weighs > 750 g. Placentomegaly can be seen in the following conditions: fetal hydrops, maternal diabetes mellitus, Rh incompatibility, chronic infections (e.g. syphilis, cytomegalovirus), maternal anaemia, or acute placental oedema with acute chorioamnionitis.

KA02.2.title: Fetus or newborn affected by placental infarction
KA02.2.definition: Placental infarction is the formation of localised areas of ischemic villous necrosis, usually due to vasospasm of the maternal circulation. The affected regions of the placenta are incompetent, and lead to placental insufficiency if the infarcts are severe.

KA02.3.title: Fetus or newborn affected by placental insufficiency or small placenta
KA02.3.definition: Placental insufficiency is defined as the inability of the placenta to deliver a sufficient supply of oxygen and nutrients to the fetus, and therefore, is unable to sustain the growth of the developing baby until term. Placental insufficiency can result in intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), pre-eclampsia, abruption, or preterm labour and delivery. A small placenta is defined as a placenta that weighs less than the lower limit of normal for the gestational period. A low placental weight can be the result of a maternal or fetal conditions. Among maternal conditions belong those causing underperfusion of the placenta, such as pre-eclampsia or maternal hypertension. Among fetal conditions belong fetal malformations or chromosomal anomalies.

KA02.4.title: Fetus or newborn affected by placental transfusion syndromes
KA02.4.definition: Twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS) occurs in monozygotic twins while they are in the uterus. It occurs when blood travels from one twin to the other, and the twin that loses blood is the donor twin, while the twin that receives blood is the recipient twin. Depending on the severity of the transfusion, both infants may experience problems, such as anaemia, paleness, and dehydration in the donor twin, and redness and an increased blood pressure in the recipient twin.

KA03.title: Fetus or newborn affected by complications of umbilical cord

KA03.0.title: Fetus or newborn affected by prolapsed cord
KA03.0.definition: A prolapsed umbilical cord is when the cord enters the opening cervix and down into the birth canal during labour before the baby has left the uterus. The risk of prolapse is higher if the baby is lying in a transverse position, the mother has had more than one baby, an excess amount of amniotic fluid exists, there is preterm prelabour rupture of membranes, or if membranes are artificially ruptured.

KA03.1.title: Fetus or newborn affected by other compression of umbilical cord
KA03.1.definition: A group of conditions characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due obstruction of blood flow through the umbilical cord secondary to pressure from an external object or misalignment of the cord itself not classified elsewhere.

KA03.2.title: Fetus or newborn affected by abnormalities of umbilical cord length

KA03.20.title: Fetus or newborn affected by short umbilical cord
KA03.20.definition: An umbilical cord < 2 SD in length below mean for the gestational age. At term, this is < 35 cm. Often associated with fetal hypokinesia

KA03.21.title: Fetus or newborn affected by long umbilical cord
KA03.21.definition: An umbilical cord > 2 SD in length above mean for the gestational age. At term, this is > 80 cm.

KA03.3.title: Fetus or newborn affected by vasa praevia
KA03.3.definition: An obstetric complication characterised by fetal vessels crossing or running in close proximity to the internal orifice of the cervix (inner cervical os).

KA03.4.title: Fetus or newborn affected by traumatic injury of the umbilical cord

KA04.title: Fetus or newborn affected by other abnormalities of membranes

KA04.0.title: Fetus or newborn affected by chorioamnionitis
KA04.0.definition: Chorioamnionitis is an infection of the placental tissues and amniotic fluid. It can lead to bacteraemia in the mother, which is an infection of the blood, and this can cause preterm birth or infection in the newborn. Organisms which are usually responsible for chorioamnionitis include Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Group B streptococcus.

KA04.1.title: Fetus or newborn affected by amniotic band syndrome

KA05.title: Fetus or newborn affected by certain complications of labour or delivery
KA05.definition: A group of conditions characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to any other adverse evolution (complication) during labour and delivery.

KA05.0.title: Fetus or newborn affected by breech delivery or extraction
KA05.0.definition: Breech presentation refers to a fetus that is lying with its bottom downwards. There are three different types of breech presentation: breech with extended legs (frank), fully flexed legs (complete), or footling (incomplete) with one or both thighs extended. Breech presentation is associated with an increased risk of intrapartum trauma or asphyxia, and caesarean section is a common mode of delivery to reduce birth-related complications.

KA05.1.title: Fetus or newborn affected by other malpresentation, malposition or disproportion during labour or delivery
KA05.1.definition: A condition characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to abnormal positions of the vertex of the fetal head (malposition) or any presentation position of the fetus other than vertex of the fetal head, first (malpresentation) during labour and delivery.

KA05.2.title: Fetus or newborn affected by forceps delivery
KA05.2.definition: A condition characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to assisted birth in which intervention assistance is provided with smooth metal instruments curved to fit around the head (forceps).

KA05.3.title: Fetus or newborn affected by delivery by vacuum extractor
KA05.3.definition: A condition characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to assisted birth in which intervention assistance is provided with a soft or hard plastic or metal cup attached by a tube to a suction device that fits firmly onto the head and attaches with suction (vacuum extractor, ventouse).

KA05.4.title: Fetus or newborn affected by caesarean delivery
KA05.4.definition: A condition characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to delivery via a surgical procedure in which one or more incisions are made through a mother's abdomen (laparotomy) and uterus (hysterotomy) to deliver one or more babies (Caesarean delivery).

KA05.5.title: Fetus or newborn affected by precipitate delivery
KA05.5.definition: A precipitate delivery is one that is < 3 hours and where contractions are unusually severe. It commonly occurs in multiparous women or when labour has been induced. Due to the force and speed of delivery, trauma may occur to the mother and newborn. The mother may suffer from haemorrhage, perineal laceration, infection, or uterine rupture, and the newborn may suffer from subdural hematoma, anoxia, or fractures.

KA05.6.title: Fetus or newborn affected by abnormal uterine contractions
KA05.6.definition: Abnormal uterine contractions can either be hypertonic or hypotonic. Hypertonic contractions are ones that occur more frequently and are marked by an increase in resting tone to more than 15 mm Hg. Hypotonic contractions are ones where the number of contractions is unusually low, the resting tone of the uterus is less than 10 mm Hg, and the strength of contractions is consistently < 26 mm Hg.

KA05.7.title: Fetus or newborn affected by abnormality in fetal intrauterine heart rate or rhythm

KA05.70.title: Fetus and newborn affected by abnormality in fetal intrauterine heart rate or rhythm before onset of labour

KA05.71.title: Fetus and newborn affected by abnormality in fetal intrauterine heart rate or rhythm during labour

KA05.8.title: Meconium passage during delivery
KA05.8.definition: Meconium passage by the fetus during labour and/or delivery process.

KA06.title: Fetus or newborn affected by noxious influences transmitted via placenta or breast milk
KA06.definition: A group of conditions characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to the transmission of any harmful or poisonous substance to the fetus or newborn via the placenta or in breast milk.

KA06.0.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal anaesthesia or analgesia in pregnancy, labour or delivery
KA06.0.definition: A condition characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to the transmission of anaesthesia or analgesia provided to the mother during the period of time between conception and childbirth.

KA06.1.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal use of tobacco
KA06.1.definition: A condition characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to the transmission of any substances derived from tobacco use by the mother to the fetus or newborn.

KA06.2.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal use of alcohol
KA06.2.definition: A condition characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to the transmission of any substances derived from alcohol use by the mother to the fetus or newborn.

KA06.3.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal use of drugs of addiction
KA06.3.definition: A condition characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to the transmission of any substances derived from other drug use by the mother to the fetus or newborn.

KA06.4.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal use of nutritional chemical substances
KA06.4.definition: A condition characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to the transmission of any substances derived from nutritional chemical use by the mother to the fetus or newborn.

KA06.5.title: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal exposure to environmental chemical substances
KA06.5.definition: A condition characterised by findings in the fetus or newborn due to the transmission of any substances derived from exposure of the mother to environmental chemicals.

KA07.title: Neonatal dermatoses due to maternal antibodies
KA07.definition: A range of antibody-mediated neonatal skin disorders due to transplacental transfer of maternal antibodies to the fetus. The relevant autoimmune disorder may or may not be apparent in the mother.

KA07.0.title: Neonatal lupus erythematosus
KA07.0.definition: Neonatal lupus erythematosus results from trans-placental transfer of maternal antibodies, in particular anti-Ro/SSA and anti La/SSB. It manifests with an erythematous rash which may be obviously photosensitive and is closely associated with congenital heart block. The mother may have known lupus, especially subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus, but she may be asymptomatic. The rash normally subsides within the first few months of life.

KA07.1.title: Neonatal pemphigus
KA07.1.definition: Neonatal pemphigus vulgaris is a short lived autoimmune skin disease arising as a result of transplacental transmission to the neonate of maternal antibodies. Neonatal pemphigus is characterised by blister formation on the skin and the mucous membranes mediated by auto-antibodies to the desmosome component desmoglein 3.

KA20.title: Disorders of newborn related to slow fetal growth or fetal malnutrition

KA20.0.title: Small for gestational age
KA20.0.definition: Birth weight below – 2 standard deviations of the mean or below the 10th percentile according to local intrauterine growth charts

KA20.00.title: Small for gestational age, symmetrical
KA20.00.definition: Growth of the fetus is affected in early pregnancy and growth is slow throughout the duration of the pregnancy. The head circumference is proportional to the rest of the body. Birth weight is 2 standard deviations below the mean, or below the 10th percentile.

KA20.01.title: Small for gestational age, asymmetrical
KA20.01.definition: This growth restriction leads to a disparity in length and head circumference when compared to birth weight. This condition typically occurs in the third trimester.

KA20.1.title: Intrauterine growth restriction
KA20.1.definition: The fetus does not achieve its predicted genetic potential and infant, not light or small for gestational age, showing signs of fetal malnutrition.

KA20.10.title: Asymmetrical intrauterine growth restriction
KA20.10.definition: There is restriction of body weight followed by length with general head sparing. This condition occurs late in pregnancy and is caused by extrinsic factors. Fetal malnutrition leading to low ponderal index less than 2 (weight to length ratio) but weight not severe enough to qualify as small for gestational age.

KA20.11.title: Symmetrical intrauterine growth restriction
KA20.11.definition: This condition begins earlier in pregnancy and there is a higher incidence of permanent neurologic sequela. It is often associated with either genetic abnormalities or fetal infection, especially 1st trimester viral infections.

KA20.12.title: Intrauterine growth restriction associated with small for gestational age
KA20.12.definition: These infants are classified as small for gestational age but have also been subject to intrauterine growth restriction.

KA20.2.title: Fetal intrauterine malnutrition without mention of small for gestational age
KA20.2.definition: Neonate, not light or small for gestational age, showing signs of fetal malnutrition, such as dry, peeling skin or loss of subcutaneous tissue.

KA21.title: Disorders of newborn related to short gestation or low birth weight, not elsewhere classified
KA21.definition: Infants whose weight is appropriate for their gestational ages are termed appropriate for gestational age (AGA). Infants that are heavier than expected are large for gestational age (LGA). Conversely, those smaller than expected are considered small for gestational age (SGA).

KA21.0.title: Extremely low birth weight of newborn
KA21.0.definition: Newborn birth weight 999 g or less. Infants have increased morbidity including neurosensory disability, cerebral palsy, retinopathy of prematurity, deafness, pulmonary immaturity, chronic lung disease and subnormal cognitive function.

KA21.00.title: Extremely low birth weight of newborn, 499g or less
KA21.00.definition: A paediatric condition in which the infant is born weighing 499 g or less.

KA21.01.title: Extremely low birth weight of newborn, 500-749g
KA21.01.definition: A paediatric condition in which the infant is born weighing between 500 and 749 g.

KA21.02.title: Extremely low birth weight of newborn, 750-999g

KA21.1.title: Very low birth weight of newborn
KA21.1.definition: A paediatric condition in which the infant is born weighing between 1000 and 1499 g.

KA21.10.title: Very low birth weight of newborn, 1000-1249g
KA21.10.definition: A paediatric condition in which the infant is born weighing between 1000 and 1249 g.

KA21.11.title: Very low birth weight of newborn, 1250-1499g
KA21.11.definition: A paediatric condition in which the infant is born weighing between 1250 and 1499 g.

KA21.2.title: Low birth weight of newborn
KA21.2.definition: A paediatric condition in which the infant is born weighing between 1500 and 2499 g.

KA21.20.title: Low birth weight of newborn, 1500-1999g
KA21.20.definition: A paediatric condition in which the infant is born weighing between 1500 and 1999 g.

KA21.21.title: Low birth weight of newborn, 2000-2499g
KA21.21.definition: A paediatric condition in which the infant is born weighing between 2000 and 2499 g.

KA21.3.title: Extreme prematurity of newborn
KA21.3.definition: Less than 28 completed weeks (less than 196 completed days) of gestation.

KA21.30.title: Extreme prematurity of newborn, gestational age less than 22 completed weeks
KA21.30.definition: Extreme prematurity of newborn, gestational age less than 22 weeks, 0 days

KA21.31.title: Extreme prematurity of newborn, gestational age 22 completed weeks
KA21.31.definition: Extreme prematurity of newborn, gestational age 22 weeks, 0 days through 22 weeks, 6 days.

KA21.32.title: Extreme prematurity of newborn, gestational age 23 completed weeks
KA21.32.definition: Extreme prematurity of newborn, gestational age 23 weeks, 0 days through 23 weeks, 6 days

KA21.33.title: Extreme prematurity of newborn, gestational age 24 completed weeks
KA21.33.definition: Extreme prematurity of newborn, gestational age 24 weeks, 0 days through 24 weeks, 6 days

KA21.34.title: Extreme prematurity of newborn, gestational age 25 completed weeks
KA21.34.definition: Extreme prematurity of newborn, gestational age 25 weeks, 0 days through 25 weeks, 6 days

KA21.35.title: Extreme prematurity of newborn, gestational age 26 completed weeks
KA21.35.definition: Extreme prematurity of newborn, gestational age 26 weeks, 0 days through 26 weeks, 6 days

KA21.36.title: Extreme prematurity of newborn, gestational age 27 completed weeks
KA21.36.definition: Extreme prematurity of newborn, gestational age 27 weeks, 0 days through 27 weeks, 6 days

KA21.4.title: Preterm newborn
KA21.4.definition: Preterm: is less than 37 completed weeks (less than 259 days) of gestation.

KA21.40.title: Preterm newborn, gestational age 28 completed weeks
KA21.40.definition: Preterm newborn, gestational age 28 weeks, 0 days through 28 weeks, 6 days

KA21.41.title: Preterm newborn, gestational age 29 completed weeks
KA21.41.definition: Preterm newborn, gestational age 29 weeks, 0 days through 29 weeks, 6 days

KA21.42.title: Preterm newborn, gestational age 30 completed weeks
KA21.42.definition: Preterm newborn, gestational age 30 weeks, 0 days through 30 weeks, 6 days

KA21.43.title: Preterm newborn, gestational age 31 completed weeks
KA21.43.definition: Preterm newborn, gestational age 31 weeks, 0 days through 31 weeks, 6 days

KA21.44.title: Preterm newborn, gestational age 32 completed weeks
KA21.44.definition: Preterm newborn, gestational age 32 weeks, 0 days through 32 weeks, 6 days

KA21.45.title: Preterm newborn, gestational age 33 completed weeks
KA21.45.definition: Preterm newborn, gestational age 33 weeks, 0 days through 33 weeks, 6 days

KA21.46.title: Preterm newborn, gestational age 34 completed weeks
KA21.46.definition: Preterm newborn, gestational age 34 weeks, 0 days through 34 weeks, 6 days

KA21.47.title: Preterm newborn, gestational age 35 completed weeks
KA21.47.definition: Preterm newborn, gestational age 35 weeks, 0 days through 35 weeks, 6 days

KA21.48.title: Preterm newborn, gestational age 36 completed weeks
KA21.48.definition: Preterm newborn, gestational age 36 weeks, 0 days through 36 weeks, 6 days

KA22.title: Disorders of newborn related to long gestation or high birth weight
KA22.definition: Usually implies gestation > 290 or 294 days (42 weeks); high birthweight = >4000g.

KA22.0.title: Exceptionally large newborn
KA22.0.definition: An exceptionally large baby is defined as having a weight at birth of > 4500 g, regardless of gestational age at birth.

KA22.1.title: Large newborn for gestational age
KA22.1.definition: A birth weight greater than the 90th percentile for gestational age or birth weight 4000-4499 g at term regardless of period of gestation.

KA22.2.title: Post-term newborn
KA22.2.definition: A condition of the newborn characterised by a gestational period that reached or exceeded 42 completed weeks (294 days or more) of gestation.

KA22.3.title: Postmaturity syndrome
KA22.3.definition: Post-term infant with signs of dysmaturity including dry peeling wrinkled skin, yellow staining of the skin, long stained fingernails, abundant scalp hair, thin growth retarded body with long thin limbs and hyperalert behaviours.

KA40.title: Birth injury to central nervous system
KA40.definition: A condition characterised by the presence of damage to the central nervous system due to physical pressure or injury during delivery.

KA40.0.title: Intracranial laceration or haemorrhage due to birth injury
KA40.0.definition: A group of conditions characterised as a traumatic brain injury occurring when the tissue of the brain is mechanically cut or torn and bleeds in a newly delivered child due to physical pressure or injury during delivery.

KA40.00.title: Subdural haemorrhage due to birth injury
KA40.00.definition: Haemorrhage into the subdural space (between the dura and the arachnoid) resulting from traumatic tearing of the bridging veins and venous sinuses due to rotational movement of the brain secondary to a traumatic delivery.

KA40.01.title: Cerebral haemorrhage due to birth injury
KA40.01.definition: Cerebral haemorrhage due to birth injury refers to haemorrhage occurring into the cerebral parenchyma as a result of birth trauma, and is commonly accompanied by extracerebral contusion and/or bleeding haemorrhage in the scalp. May have associated skull fracture(s).

KA40.02.title: Cerebellar haemorrhage due to birth injury
KA40.02.definition: Haemorrhage into the cerebellum, hemispheres or vermis, due to trauma. Occipitaloseodiastasis with breech delivery is the most common cause of this injury.

KA40.03.title: Intraventricular haemorrhage due to birth injury
KA40.03.definition: Traumatic haemorrhage into the intraventricular space as the dominant lesion, usually in a term infant, a result of birth trauma. Usually seen in conjunction with other intracranial bleeding (parenchymal, subdural, subarachnoid) and can be seen in the term or preterm infant.

KA40.04.title: Subarachnoid haemorrhage due to birth injury
KA40.04.definition: Haemorrhage within the subarachnoid space (the area between the arachnoid membrane and the pia matter) due to either leakage from the leptomeningeal plexus or rupture of bridging veins within the subarachnoid space.

KA40.05.title: Tentorial tear due to birth injury
KA40.05.definition: Lacerations of tentorium cerebelli due to birth trauma, usually resulting in infratentorial haemorrhages; lesser degrees of tentorial injury most commonly associated with subdural bleeds.

KA40.06.title: Cerebellar contusion due to birth injury
KA40.06.definition: A bruise of the brain tissue. There is a punctuate haemorrhage which occurs in the long gyri.

KA40.07.title: Cerebral contusion due to birth injury
KA40.07.definition: A bruise of the brain tissue. Focal region of necrosis and haemorrhage, usually involving the cerebral cortex and subcortical white matter

KA40.08.title: Extradural or epidural haemorrhage due to birth injury
KA40.08.definition: Haemorrhage in the plane between the skull bone and the periosteum on the inner surface of the skull from injury to the middle meningeal artery from birth trauma

KA40.1.title: Cerebral oedema due to birth injury
KA40.1.definition: Cerebral oedema is an excessive accumulation of water in the intracellular or extracellular spaces of the brain. There is a breakdown of the tight endothelial junctions which make up the blood brain barrier.

KA40.2.title: Birth injury to spine or spinal cord
KA40.2.definition: Injury to the spinal cord incurred during delivery from excessive traction or rotation, principally occurring during breech and rotational forceps during vertex deliveries

KA40.3.title: Birth injury to brainstem
KA40.3.definition: Injury to the brain stem occurring during delivery due to excessive longitudinal traction especially when this traction is combined with flexion and torsion of the spine during delivery.

KA41.title: Birth injury to eye
KA41.definition: Ocular injuries due to birth trauma include lid lacerations, hyphema, rupture of Descemet's membrane of cornea, vitreous haemorrhage, corneal oedema, abrasions and lacerations, orbital haemorrhage and fractures, and intraocular haemorrhages.

KA42.title: Birth injury to scalp
KA42.definition: A condition characterised by the presence of damage to the scalp due to physical pressure or injury during delivery.

KA42.0.title: Bruising of scalp due to birth injury
KA42.0.definition: Erythema of the scalp occurring usually as a result of dystocia or application of forceps

KA42.1.title: Cephalohaematoma due to birth injury
KA42.1.definition: Cephalhaematoma is a subperiosteal collection of blood caused by rupture of vessels beneath the periosteum and does not extend across the suture lines.

KA42.2.title: Chignon due to birth injury
KA42.2.definition: Chignon is a temporary swelling (oedema of the scalp) secondary to the placement of a ventouse suction cup used in assisted vacuum deliveries. It usually disappears after several hours

KA42.3.title: Monitoring injury of scalp of newborn
KA42.3.definition: Injuries to the scalp from use of intrapartum fetal monitoring devices including injury following fetal blood sampling.

KA42.4.title: Subgaleal epicranial subaponeurotic haemorrhage due to birth injury
KA42.4.definition: Subgaleal haemorrhage is a collection of blood in the space between the epicranial aponeurosis of the scalp and the periosteum of the skull.

KA43.title: Birth injury to skin or soft tissues
KA43.definition: Superficial injury including abrasions, lacerations and ecchymoses sustained during birth to sites other than scalp face or external genitalia.

KA43.0.title: Birth injury to sternocleidomastoid
KA43.0.definition: Injury to the sternomastoid muscle due to birth usually presents with torticollis (tilt and rotation of head) and a firm, spindle-shaped, immobile mass in the midportion of sternomastoid muscle.

KA43.1.title: Birth injury to external genitalia
KA43.1.definition: Injuries of external genitalia such as oedema, ecchymoses, or haematomas of scrotum or labia majora, haematocoele, or trauma to the testes as a result of trauma during birth, especially after a breech delivery.

KA43.2.title: Subcutaneous fat necrosis due to birth injury
KA43.2.definition: Subcutaneous fat necrosis is a rare acute transient hypodermatitis that develops within first weeks of life in term infants.

KA43.3.title: Birth injury to face
KA43.3.definition: Birth injuries to face include injuries sustained to nose (deviations, deformities, or septal damage), ears (abrasions, lacerations, deformities or haematomas).

KA44.title: Birth injury to peripheral nervous system
KA44.definition: A condition characterised by the presence of damage to the nerves or ganglia outside of the brain or spinal cord due to physical pressure or injury during delivery.

KA44.0.title: Birth injury to cranial nerves
KA44.0.definition: Birth injuries to the cranial nerves include contusion, avulsion, rupture, neuroma or praxis.

KA44.00.title: Birth injury to facial nerve
KA44.00.definition: Facial palsy involving both upper and lower halves of the face caused by traumatic compression of the facial nerve as it exits the stylomastoid foramen, or as it passes over the ramus of the mandible.

KA44.1.title: Brachial plexus palsy in newborn
KA44.1.definition: Brachial plexus birth palsy occurs when the brachial plexus are damaged during birth. It occurs most typically during a difficult delivery.

KA44.10.title: Erb paralysis
KA44.10.definition: Erb paralysis is one of the most common brachial plexus birth palsy. The injury occurs in the upper brachial plexus nerves and affects the upper arm.

KA44.11.title: Klumpke paralysis
KA44.11.definition: Klumpke paralysis is a form of brachial plexus palsy that causes paralysis in the hand.

KA44.2.title: Phrenic nerve paralysis due to birth injury
KA44.2.definition: Birth injury to the cervical roots 3 to 5 resulting in the paralysis of the ipsilateral diaphragm usually after a difficult breech delivery

KA45.title: Birth injury to skeleton
KA45.definition: A condition characterised by the presence of damage to the skeleton due to physical pressure or injury during delivery.

KA45.0.title: Fracture of skull due to birth injury
KA45.0.definition: Linear or depressed fractures of skull bones resulting from injury during birth, including those related to forceps or vacuum assisted delivery.

KA45.00.title: Linear skull fracture due to birth injury
KA45.00.definition: Linear fractures of skull bones resulting from injury during birth, including those related to forceps and vacuum assisted delivery.

KA45.01.title: Depressed skull fracture due to birth injury
KA45.01.definition: Depressed fractures of skull bones resulting from injury during birth, including those related to forceps and vacuum assisted delivery

KA45.1.title: Occipital osteodiastasis due to birth injury
KA45.1.definition: Occipital osteodiastasis (OOD) is a form of birth injury characterised by a tear along the innominate (posterior occipital or supraoccipital-exoccipital) synchondrosis with separation of the occipital squama from the lateral or condylar parts of the occipital bone.

KA45.20.title: Mandibular bone fracture due to birth injury

KA45.21.title: Nasal bone fracture due to birth injury

KA45.3.title: Birth injury of thorax
KA45.3.definition: Fracture of bones of the thorax including ribs, sternum due to birth injury.

KA45.4.title: Fracture, dislocation or subluxation of spine due to birth injury
KA45.4.definition: A true fracture of the spine is very rare due to birth injury. A fracture is usually in the cervical area and follows a difficult footling breech vaginal delivery. Dislocation refers to the displacement of one of the cervical vertebra relative to another in the cervical spine. The trauma allows one vertebra to shift position over the vertebra below. If this dislocation is partial the term “subluxation” is used. The injury to the spine may be unilateral or bilateral. Dislocations may be stable or unstable referring to the degree of mobility and the extent of additional damage to the supporting ligaments.

KA45.5.title: Fracture of clavicle due to birth injury
KA45.5.definition: This is a greenstick fracture of the clavicle that may occur during the birthing process.

KA46.title: Birth injury to other organs
KA46.definition: A group of conditions characterised by the presence of damage of organs of a newly delivered child due to physical pressure or injury during delivery.

KA46.0.title: Birth injury to liver
KA46.0.definition: Rupture or subcapsular haemorrhage into the liver parenchyma as a result of birth trauma usually seen in large for gestational age infants, those with hepatomegaly, those born by breech delivery; may present as haemoperitoneum

KA46.1.title: Birth injury to spleen
KA46.1.definition: Rupture or subcapsular haemorrhage into spleen as a result of birth trauma; may present as haemoperitoneum

KA46.2.title: Adrenal haemorrhage due to birth injury

KA61.title: Other bacterial infections of the fetus or newborn

KA61.0.title: Congenital tuberculosis
KA61.0.definition: A disease affecting infants, caused by an infection with the bacteria Mycobacterium tuberculosis in utero. Transmission is by vertical transmission.

KA61.1.title: Neonatal listeriosis
KA61.1.definition: A condition affecting fetuses or neonates, caused by an infection with the gram-positive bacteria Listeria. This condition is characterised by respiratory distress in the neonate, by stillbirth, or by abortion. Transmission is by vertical transmission. Confirmation is by identification of Listeria in the neonate and mother.

KA62.title: Viral infection in the fetus or newborn
KA62.definition: Any condition affecting fetuses or newborns, caused by an infection with a virus.

KA62.1.title: Congenital Epstein-Barr virus infection
KA62.1.definition: There are several forms of Epstein–Barr virus infection. Infectious mononucleosis, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and Burkitt's lymphoma can all be caused by the Epstein–Barr virus.

KA62.2.title: Congenital Varicella Zoster virus infection
KA62.2.definition: Transplacentally acquired Varicella zoster virus infection. Both the gestational age at the time of maternal infection and the time interval between maternal infection and birth have major influences on the clinical course.

KA62.3.title: Congenital cytomegalovirus infection
KA62.3.definition: A condition affecting neonates, caused by an infection with cytomegalovirus in utero. This condition is characterised by jaundice, low birth weight, splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, or pneumonia if symptoms develop shortly after birth, or may be asymptomatic. This condition commonly presents later in life with loss of hearing, loss of vision, or developmental disabilities. Transmission is by vertical transmission. Confirmation is by detection of cytomegalovirus in neonatal urine, saliva, blood, or other body tissues within 2-3 weeks of birth.

KA62.4.title: Congenital echovirus infection
KA62.4.definition: A disease affecting neonates, caused by an infection with enteric cytopathic human orphan (ECHO) virus in utero. This disease presents with various symptoms depending on the site of the infection, or may be asymptomatic. Transmission is by vertical transmission. Confirmation is by identification of ECHO virus in the neonate.

KA62.5.title: Congenital enterovirus infection
KA62.5.definition: Congenital viral infections with enteroviruses (including coxsackie viruses and ECHO viruses) are infectious embryofetopathies that have been reported to cause fetal malformations, acute systemic illness in the newborn and long-term neurodevelopmental abnormalities.

KA62.6.title: Congenital human immunodeficiency virus infection
KA62.6.definition: A disease affecting neonates, caused by an infection with human immunodeficiency virus in utero. Transmission is by vertical transmission. Confirmation is by identification of human immunodeficiency virus in the neonate.

KA62.7.title: Congenital parvovirus syndrome
KA62.7.definition: Fetal parvovirus syndrome is a fetopathy likely to occur when a pregnant woman is infected by parvovirus B19. Fetal parvovirus infection results in aplastic crisis. Anaemia induces a risk of hydrops and fetal death by cardiac failure in 10 to 20% of cases.

KA62.8.title: Congenital rubella syndrome
KA62.8.definition: A disease caused by an infection with the rubella virus in utero. This disease presents with symptoms depending on the timing of infection of the fetus and may present with birth defects (such as hearing loss), or intrauterine growth retardation. Transmission is by vertical transmission. Confirmation is by identification of rubella virus or detection of anti-rubella virus IgM antibodies in the neonate or infant.

KA62.9.title: Congenital viral hepatitis
KA62.9.definition: A disease of the liver affecting the neonate, caused by an infection with either hepatitis A, B, C, D, or E virus in utero. This disease is characterised by lethargy, jaundice, abdominal distention, failure to thrive, or clay coloured stools. Transmission is by vertical transmission. Confirmation is by identification of the hepatitis A, B, C, D, or E virus in a blood sample from the neonate.

KA62.A.title: Perinatal Herpes simplex infection
KA62.A.definition: Herpes simplex infection acquired during the perinatal period, normally from active herpes infection of the mother's genital tract, but may also be transmitted in utero.

KA63.title: Fungal infection of fetus or newborn
KA63.definition: Any condition affecting fetuses or newborns, caused by an infection with a fungal agent.

KA63.0.title: Malassezia infection in newborn
KA63.0.definition: A condition affecting newborns, caused by an infection with Malassezia that leads to a severe systemic inflammatory response. This condition is characterised by fever or respiratory distress. Confirmation is by identification of Malassezia in a blood sample.

KA63.1.title: Neonatal aspergillosis
KA63.1.definition: A disease affecting neonates, caused by an infection with the fungi Aspergillus. This disease presents with clinical symptoms depending on the site of infection. Transmission is by inhalation of Aspergillus spores, or direct contact. Confirmation is by identification of Aspergillus from affected sites.

KA63.2.title: Neonatal candidosis
KA63.2.definition: A condition affecting neonates, caused by an infection with the fungi Candida. This condition is characterised by apnoea, thrombocytopenia, or decreasing respiratory function or other symptoms depending on the site of infection. Transmission is vertical (from the mother to the baby). Confirmation is by identification of Candida in a blood or urine sample.

KA64.title: Parasitic diseases in the fetus or newborn
KA64.definition: Any condition affecting fetuses or newborns, caused by an infection with a parasite.

KA64.0.title: Congenital toxoplasmosis
KA64.0.definition: A disease caused by an infection with the protozoan parasite Toxoplasma gondii in utero. This disease is characterised by chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, intracranial calcifications, anaemia, or neurological deficits that develop after birth. This disease may present at birth with jaundice, premature birth, hepatosplenomegaly, myocarditis, pneumonitis, or rash. Transmission is by vertical transmission. In the fetus, confirmation is by identification of Toxoplasma gondii in amniotic fluid; in the neonate, confirmation is by identification of Toxoplasma gondii in body fluids or tissues, or detection of antibodies against Toxoplasma gondii.

KA64.20.title: Congenital falciparum malaria
KA64.20.definition: A disease caused by an infection with the protozoan parasite Plasmodium falciparum in utero. This disease is characterised by fever, anaemia, splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, jaundice, regurgitation, diarrhoea, or poor feeding. This disease may also present with respiratory distress, drowsiness, or cyanosis. Transmission is by vertical transmission. Confirmation is by identification of the Plasmodium falciparum in a blood sample from the neonate.

KA64.21.title: Congenital non-falciparum malaria
KA64.21.definition: Congenital malaria due to Plasmodium species other than Plasmodium falciparum. For example, Plasmodium vivax infects fetuses transplacentally, causing congenital malaria that can lead to anaemia and low birth weight.

KA65.title: Neonatal infections of certain specified sites

KA65.0.title: Neonatal conjunctivitis or dacryocystitis
KA65.0.definition: This refers to inflammation of the conjunctiva (the outermost layer of the eye and the inner surface of the eyelids) and the inflammation of the nasolacrimal sac, frequently caused by nasolacrimal duct obstruction or infection.

KA65.1.title: Omphalitis of newborn
KA65.1.definition: A disease of the umbilical cord affecting newborns, commonly caused by an infection with a bacterial source. This disease is characterised by purulent or foul-smelling discharge from the umbilicus or umbilical stump, periumbilical erythema, oedema, or tenderness. This disease may also present with fever, hypothermia, jaundice, tachycardia, hypotension, tachypnoea, respiratory distress, apnoea, or abdominal distention with absent bowel sounds. Transmission is by vertical transmission or iatrogenic transmission. Confirmation is by identification of the infectious agent.

KA65.2.title: Neonatal urinary tract infection
KA65.2.definition: A condition of the urinary tract affecting neonates, commonly caused by an infection with a bacterial source. This condition is characterised by fever, pyuria, jaundice, poor appetite, diarrhoea, blood tinged stool, vomiting, or abdominal distention. This condition may also be asymptomatic. Transmission is by vertical transmission. Confirmation is by identification of the infectious agent in a urine sample.

KA65.3.title: Neonatal infectious mastitis
KA65.3.definition: A disease of the breasts in neonates, may be caused by a maternal infection with a bacterial source. This disease is characterised by swelling, erythema, warmth, tenderness, induration of the breast, or purulent discharge from the nipple. It is usually unilateral. This disease may also present with breast abscesses.

KA80.title: Fetal blood loss
KA80.definition: Fetal blood loss is a loss of blood from the fetal circulation during pregnancy, labour, or delivery. Due to the small volume of fetal blood that is present, even a small loss can lead to anaemia or fetal death.

KA80.0.title: Fetal blood loss from vasa praevia
KA80.0.definition: In vasa praevia, the fetal blood vessels connecting the placenta and umbilical cord cross the internal cervical os, the entrance to the birth canal, underneath the fetus. These vessels are more liable to be injured by instrumentation (e.g. scalp electrode, intrauterine pressure catheter, vaginal exams) or simply due to the normal mechanical forces of labour leading to serious fetal blood loss.

KA80.1.title: Fetal blood loss from ruptured cord
KA80.1.definition: The umbilical cord can rupture during labour and delivery and lead to fetal blood loss. Possible reasons include: traction on an abnormally short cord, a cord that is entangled around the fetus, a thin friable cord, or a cord with vascular abnormalities. Fetal blood loss can also occur following accidental cord puncture during amniocentesis or following in utero cordocentesis or transfusion.

KA80.2.title: Fetal blood loss from placenta
KA80.2.definition: Fetal blood loss can result from placental abruption, which is when the placenta separates from the uterine wall prior to delivery. Placental abruptions occur under conditions of maternal hypertension and drug use (e.g. cocaine), maternal vascular and collagen vascular disease, maternal clotting disorders, and following direct abdominal trauma. Fetal blood loss can also result from accidental incision of the placenta during a caesarean section.

KA80.3.title: Haemorrhage into co-twin
KA80.3.definition: Monozygous twins often share a placenta. Vascular anastomoses within the placenta allow for the transfer of blood between the two fetuses. In some cases, the flow is unbalanced and one fetus (larger, plethoric, and polycythaemic twin) has an overload of fluid, while the other (smaller, hydropic twin) becomes anaemic.

KA80.4.title: Haemorrhage into maternal circulation
KA80.4.definition: Fetal-maternal haemorrhage occurs when the trophoblastic lining of the placenta fails to act as a barrier and allows fetal blood cells to enter the maternal circulation.

KA80.5.title: Fetal blood loss from cut end of co-twin cord
KA80.5.definition: Sometimes the blood content of monozygotic twins differs considerably, which can occur when anastomoses exist. One twin loses blood through shunts, while the other gains a large quantity of blood. Therefore, following the delivery of one twin, the other may bleed through these anastomoses if the umbilical cord of the delivered twin is not immediately clamped.

KA81.title: Umbilical haemorrhage of newborn
KA81.definition: A condition characterised by bleeding from the umbilical cord stump of a newborn.

KA82.title: Intracranial nontraumatic haemorrhage of fetus or newborn
KA82.definition: Intraventricular (nontraumatic) haemorrhage of the fetus and newborn is a condition characterised by bleeding within the skull of a newborn that is not due to injury causing physical damage.

KA82.0.title: Intraventricular nontraumatic haemorrhage, grade 1, of fetus or newborn
KA82.0.definition: A condition characterised by bleeding into the subependymal region or germinal matrix of the ventricular system of the brain of a newborn that is not due to injury causing physical damage.

KA82.1.title: Intraventricular nontraumatic haemorrhage, grade 2, of fetus or newborn
KA82.1.definition: Intraventricular (nontraumatic) haemorrhage, grade 2 is a condition of the fetus or newborn characterised by bleeding into the germinal matrix of the ventricular system with bleeding into the lateral ventricles of the brain without ventricular enlargement.

KA82.2.title: Intraventricular nontraumatic haemorrhage, grade 3, of fetus or newborn
KA82.2.definition: Intraventricular (nontraumatic) haemorrhage, grade 3, of the fetus and newborn located in the subependymal region with extension into the lateral ventricles, with ventricular enlargement.

KA82.3.title: Intraventricular nontraumatic haemorrhage, grade 4, of fetus or newborn

KA82.4.title: Intracerebral nontraumatic haemorrhage of fetus or newborn
KA82.4.definition: A condition characterised by bleeding within the brain tissue of a fetus or newborn that is not due to injury causing physical damage.

KA82.5.title: Subarachnoid nontraumatic haemorrhage of fetus or newborn
KA82.5.definition: A condition characterised by bleeding into the area between the arachnoid membrane and the pia mater (subarachnoid space) surrounding the brain of a fetus or newborn that is not due to injury causing physical damage.

KA82.6.title: Cerebellar nontraumatic, hemispheres or vermis or posterior fossa haemorrhage of fetus or newborn
KA82.6.definition: A condition characterised by bleeding within the part of the intracranial cavity located between the foramen magnum and tentorium cerebelli (posterior fossa) including bleeding in tissue of the cerebellum or brain stem, of a fetus or newborn that is not due to injury causing physical damage.

KA82.7.title: Subdural nontraumatic haemorrhage of fetus or newborn

KA83.title: Certain specified neonatal haemorrhages
KA83.definition: Any other condition characterised by bleeding in a newborn.

KA83.0.title: Neonatal bleeding originating in the mouth, nose or pharynx

KA83.00.title: Neonatal epistaxis
KA83.00.definition: A condition characterised by bleeding from the nose of a newborn.

KA83.1.title: Neonatal bleeding originating in the oesophagus, stomach, small or large intestine
KA83.1.definition: Bleeding in the neonate that originates from the digestive system. Most common causes include enteritis, gastritis, milk protein allergies, intussusception, and/or erosions of mucosa.

KA83.2.title: Neonatal rectal haemorrhage
KA83.2.definition: A condition characterised by bleeding in the rectum of a newborn.

KA83.3.title: Neonatal hepatic haemorrhage
KA83.3.definition: Haemorrhage of the liver in the newborn.

KA83.4.title: Neonatal haemorrhage originating in adrenal gland
KA83.4.definition: A condition characterised by bleeding into the adrenal glands in a newborn.

KA83.6.title: Neonatal haemorrhage originating in kidney or bladder

KA83.7.title: Neonatal haemorrhage originating in trachea or pulmonary parenchyma

KA83.9.title: Neonatal vaginal or uterine haemorrhage
KA83.9.definition: A condition characterised by bleeding from the vagina of a newborn which is excessive or lasts longer than the first month of life.

KA84.title: Haemolytic disease of fetus or newborn
KA84.definition: A paediatric alloimmune condition characterised by the break-down of red blood cells by IgG antibodies which are transmitted from mother to child via the placenta.

KA84.0.title: Rh isoimmunization of fetus or newborn
KA84.0.definition: A condition characterised by the transmission of antibodies from a mother to the child via the placenta against the Rhesus factor of blood. Such antibodies were developed in a Rhesus factor negative mother subsequent to exposure to Rhesus factor positive blood resulting in the break-down of the red blood cells of the fetus.

KA84.1.title: Isoimmunization due to other red cell factors

KA84.2.title: ABO isoimmunization of fetus or newborn
KA84.2.definition: A condition of the newborn characterized by the destruction of red blood cells initiated by the transmission of anti-A or anti-B antibodies from a mother to the child via the placenta against A or B antigens of the newborn's blood.

KA84.3.title: Haemolytic anaemia due to other unclassified antibodies of fetus or newborn

KA84.4.title: Haemolytic disease due to disease of other neonatal organs

KA84.5.title: Neonatal haemolysis due to systemic bacterial infection with or without concomitant diffuse intravascular coagulation

KA85.title: Hydrops fetalis due to haemolytic disease
KA85.definition: A fetal condition characterised by an accumulation of fluid or oedema in at least two fetal compartments, including subcutaneous compartments, the pleura, the pericardium, or the abdomen, due to the antibody-mediated break-down of fetal red blood cells.

KA85.0.title: Hydrops fetalis due to isoimmunization
KA85.0.definition: A fetal condition characterised by an accumulation of fluid or oedema in at least two fetal compartments, including subcutaneous compartments, the pleura, the pericardium, or the abdomen, due to the transmission of IgG antibodies against the Rhesus factor of blood from the mother to the child via the placenta that break-down of the red blood cells of the fetus.

KA86.title: Neonatal kernicterus
KA86.definition: Kernicterus is a pathologic diagnosis of the neonate that is characterised by yellow staining of the basal ganglia following elevated bilirubin concentrations in the blood and/or a breech in the blood brain barrier more common in the premature infant or the sick term neonate. It is characterised later in infancy and childhood by hearing deficits, choreoathetosis, and varying degrees of cognitive deficit.

KA87.title: Neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia
KA87.definition: A condition characterised as an increased level of bilirubin above 85 µmol/l (5 mg/dL) which manifests as yellowing of the eyes, skin, and other tissues of a newborn due to excessive break-down of red blood cells for any other reason not classified elsewhere.

KA87.0.title: Neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia due to swallowed maternal blood
KA87.0.definition: A condition characterised as an increased level of bilirubin above 85 umol/l (5 mg/dL) which manifests as yellowing of the eyes, skin, and other tissues of a newborn due consumption by the newborn of blood from the mother.

KA87.1.title: Neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia due to enzymatic defect in bilirubin degradation

KA87.2.title: Neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia due to breast milk inhibitor of bilirubin conjugation
KA87.2.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by persistently increased level of bilirubin above 85 umol/l (5 mg/dL) manifesting as yellowing of the eyes, skin, and other tissues of a newborn due to any chemical substance that prevents or decreases the production of breast milk by the mother.

KA87.3.title: Neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia due to total parenteral nutrition
KA87.3.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by persistently increased level of bilirubin above 85 umol/l (5 mg/dL) manifesting as yellowing of the eyes, skin, and other tissues of a newborn due to intravenous feeding which bypasses the normal processes of eating and digestion.

KA87.4.title: Neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia due to drugs or toxins transmitted from mother

KA87.5.title: Neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia due to drugs or toxins given to newborn

KA87.6.title: Neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia from other or unspecified hepatocellular damage

KA88.title: Disseminated intravascular coagulation of fetus or newborn
KA88.definition: Neonatal purpura fulminans is a potentially lethal disorder characterised by progressive haemorrhagic necrosis of the skin associated with cutaneous vascular thrombosis. It is usually due to a genetically transmitted thrombophilic disorder: most commonly homozygous deficiency of protein C or, less frequently, protein S.

KA89.title: Transient neonatal thrombocytopaenia
KA89.definition: A rare paediatric condition characterised by a temporary relative decrease in the number of platelets in the blood associated with either increased destruction or decreased production of platelets in a newborn.

KA89.0.title: Thrombocytopaenia following systemic infection, including diffuse intravascular coagulation

KA8A.title: Polycythaemia neonatorum
KA8A.definition: Polycythaemia of the neonate represents an excessive quality of circulating red blood cells due to excessive marrow production and haematocrits that exceed ~60%.

KA8A.0.title: Polycythaemia neonatorum due to placental insufficiency or fetal intrauterine growth restriction

KA8A.1.title: Polycythaemia neonatorum due to twin to twin transfusion

KA8A.2.title: Polycythaemia neonatorum due to inherited disorder of erythropoietin production

KA8A.3.title: Polycythaemia neonatorum following umbilical cord transfusion or stripping at delivery

KA8B.title: Anaemia of prematurity
KA8B.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by a decrease in number of red blood cells (RBCs) or less than the normal quantity of haemoglobin in the blood of a newborn associated with the child being born prior to completing 37 weeks of gestation.

KA8C.title: Congenital hypoplastic anaemia
KA8C.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by a decreased number of red blood cells (RBCs) or lower than the normal levels of haemoglobin in the blood of a newborn present at birth due to loss of blood from the circulatory system of the fetus.

KA8D.title: Transient neonatal neutropaenia
KA8D.definition: Neonatal neutropaenia can be due to underproduction of the marrow (e.g. hypoxemia due to placental insufficiency, congenital viral disease) or excessive utilization of white blood cells (bacterial sepsis) or due to maternal transfer of antibodies to the fetus

KA8E.title: Alloimmune neonatal neutropaenia
KA8E.definition: Alloimmune neonatal neutropaenia (ANN) is a disease caused by the passive transfer of neutrophil specific maternal IgG antibodies across the placenta during pregnancy.

KA8F.title: Neonatal vitamin K deficiency
KA8F.definition: There are 3 forms of vitamin K–deficiency bleeding (VKDB) of the newborn. Early VKDB (haemorrhagic disease of the newborn) that occurs at 1-14 days of age. The most common sites of bleeding are the gastrointestinal tract, mucosal and cutaneous tissue, the umbilical stump, and the post-circumcision site. Late VKDB most commonly occurs at 2-12 weeks of age, although cases can occur up to 6 months. The most common site of bleeding is intracranial, although cutaneous and gastrointestinal bleeding may be initial manifestation. The third form of VKDB occurs at birth or shortly thereafter. It is secondary to maternal intake of medications (warfarin, phenobarbital, phenytoin) that cross the placenta.

KA8F.0.title: Diffuse bleeding diathesis due to vitamin K deficient haemorrhagic disease of fetus or newborn
KA8F.0.definition: Haemorrhagic disease of the newborn is a bleeding disorder of the newborn usually seen in the first week after life when vitamin K replacement is not provided to the newborn infant immediately after birth and is primarily characterised by gastrointestinal bleeding. The disorder can also be seen later in the newborn period in breast fed infants of vitamin K deficient mothers.

KB00.title: Neonatal cerebral ischaemia
KB00.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by insufficient blood flow to the brain of a newborn to meet metabolic demand.

KB01.title: Periventricular cysts of newborn
KB01.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by the development of cysts around the brain ventricles in a newborn.

KB02.title: Neonatal cerebral leukomalacia
KB02.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by the death of small areas of brain tissue creating "holes" in the brain of a newborn.

KB03.title: Neonatal encephalopathy, not elsewhere classified
KB03.definition: Encephalopathy is disorder of the brain. It may be the result of interference in the development of the brain, an infection or other condition in the neonate.

KB04.title: Hypoxic ischaemic encephalopathy of newborn
KB04.definition: Hypoxic ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE) is when a newborn’s brain fails to receive a sufficient amount of oxygen or blood before and during birth that may lead to brain damage or death.

KB06.title: Neonatal seizures
KB06.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by rapid and repeated muscle contraction and relaxation, resulting in an uncontrolled shaking of the body of a newborn.

KB08.title: Disorders of muscle tone of newborn
KB08.definition: A group of paediatric conditions characterised by abnormal muscle tone in a newborn.

KB08.0.title: Transient neonatal myasthenia gravis
KB08.0.definition: A paediatric condition characterised as a temporary autoimmune neuromuscular disease leading to fluctuating muscle weakness and fatigue in a newborn.

KB08.1.title: Congenital hypertonia
KB08.1.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by abnormally increased muscle tone that is present at birth in a newborn.

KB08.2.title: Congenital hypotonia
KB08.2.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by abnormally decreased muscle tone that is present at birth in a newborn.

KB20.title: Intrauterine hypoxia
KB20.definition: Intrauterine hypoxia occurs when the fetus is deprived of an adequate supply of oxygen. This may occur with prolapse or occlusion of the umbilical cord, placental infarction and maternal smoking. This can lead to damage of the central nervous system and neonatal encephalopathy, which increases the risk of mortality.

KB20.0.title: Intrauterine hypoxia first noted before onset of labour
KB20.0.definition: A condition characterised by deprivation of an adequate supply of oxygen to the fetus during the gestation period which is diagnosed prior to the onset of labour.

KB20.1.title: Intrauterine hypoxia first noted during labour or delivery
KB20.1.definition: A condition characterised by deprivation of an adequate supply of oxygen to the fetus diagnosed immediately prior to or during labour and delivery.

KB21.0.title: Severe birth asphyxia
KB21.0.definition: Pulse less than 100 per minute at birth and falling or steady, respiration absent or gasping, colour poor, tone absent.

KB21.1.title: Mild and moderate birth asphyxia
KB21.1.definition: Normal respiration not established within one minute, but heart rate 100 or above, some muscle tone present, some response to stimulation.

KB22.title: Metabolic acidaemia in newborn
KB22.definition: Metabolic acidaemia represents an increase in hydrogen ion concentration, usually due to the production of lactic acid following hypoxia or ischemia induced anaerobic metabolism. Acidaemia can also result from inborn errors of metabolism, and disorders of the kidney and liver.

KB23.title: Respiratory distress of newborn
KB23.definition: A condition characterised by developmental insufficiency of surfactant associated proteins or surfactant production and structural immaturity in the lungs.

KB23.0.title: Respiratory distress syndrome of newborn
KB23.0.definition: Respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) is an acute illness, usually of preterm infants, due to pulmonary surfactant deficiency, developing within 4-6 hours of birth, and is characterised by respiratory distress (tachypnoea, intercostal and sternal retractions, expiratory grunt, and cyanosis) with abnormal chest radiograph showing diffuse reticulogranular densities and air bronchograms, evidence of reduced lung compliance and functional residual capacity, evidence of abnormal gas exchange (hypoxaemia, hypercapnia, cyanosis) of sufficient severity to require oxygen and/or continuous or intermittent positive pressure ventilatory support for more than 24 hours.

KB23.00.title: Respiratory distress syndrome of the newborn, altered by maternal corticosteroid therapy

KB23.01.title: Respiratory distress syndrome of the newborn, altered by pulmonary surfactant replacement therapy

KB23.02.title: Respiratory distress syndrome of the newborn, altered by maternal corticosteroid therapy or pulmonary surfactant replacement therapy

KB23.1.title: Transient tachypnoea of newborn
KB23.1.definition: Transient tachypnoea of newborn is usually a benign self-limiting illness of term and near-term infants demonstrating increased respiratory rate and requiring supplementary oxygen after birth.

KB23.2.title: Respiratory instability of prematurity
KB23.2.definition: Infant within the neonatal period who requires continued respiratory life support, including positive pressure ventilation and/or prolonged oxygen therapy, without a clear pathologic diagnosis. This may be caused by inadequate respiratory muscle strength, excessive chest wall compliance, and/or inadequate CNS respiratory drive.

KB24.title: Congenital pneumonia
KB24.definition: Congenital pneumonia is an acute respiratory infection contracted prenatally or during the intrapartum period that is caused by a virus, bacteria, or fungi.

KB25.title: Neonatal tracheitis
KB25.definition: A disease of the trachea in neonates, caused by an infection with a bacterial, viral, or fungal source. This disease is characterised by stridor, or increased respiratory effort. Transmission is commonly by inhalation of the infectious agent. Confirmation is by direct laryngoscopy.

KB26.title: Neonatal aspiration syndromes
KB26.definition: Aspiration of meconium, blood, amniotic fluids and gastric contents in a neonate resulting in clinical symptoms from airway obstruction (atelectasis, air trapping and air leaks), parenchymal injury (pneumonitis), right-to-left shunting, and ventilation-perfusion mismatch.

KB26.0.title: Neonatal aspiration of meconium
KB26.0.definition: Meconium Aspiration Syndrome (MAS) is defined as respiratory distress in an infant born through meconium-stained amniotic fluid with roentgenographic findings consistent with MAS and whose symptoms could not be otherwise explained.

KB26.1.title: Neonatal aspiration of amniotic fluid or mucus
KB26.1.definition: Clinical symptoms of Neonatal aspiration syndrome due to inhalation of amniotic fluid

KB26.2.title: Neonatal aspiration of blood
KB26.2.definition: Clinical symptoms of Neonatal aspiration syndrome due to inhalation of blood usually during birth process, or through aspiration of gastrointestinal bleeding.

KB26.3.title: Neonatal aspiration of milk or regurgitated food
KB26.3.definition: Clinical symptoms of Neonatal aspiration syndrome due to aspiration of acidic gastric content and/or milk.

KB27.title: Pulmonary air leak or related conditions originating in the perinatal period
KB27.definition: Clinical syndrome due to free air from rupture of overdistended alveoli tracking into pulmonary interstitium, mediastinum, pleural cavity or subcutaneous tissues.

KB27.0.title: Interstitial emphysema originating in the perinatal period
KB27.0.definition: Escape of air into the interstitium, lymphatics and venous circulation of the lungs resulting from rupture of small airways associated with a characteristic cystic appearance on chest X-ray, almost exclusively seen in preterm infants receiving mechanical ventilation

KB27.1.title: Pneumothorax originating in the perinatal period
KB27.1.definition: Abnormal presence of air or other gas in the pleural cavity, usually secondary to tracking of free air from pulmonary interstitial emphysema, or rupture of subpleural blebs.

KB27.2.title: Pneumomediastinum originating in the perinatal period
KB27.2.definition: Presence of air in the mediastinum usually from tracking of free air from ruptured alveolar ducts along the perivascular sheaths of pulmonary blood vessels, or rupture of subpleural bleb

KB27.3.title: Pneumopericardium originating in the perinatal period
KB27.3.definition: Presence of air in the pericardial cavity usually from tracking of free air from ruptured alveolar ducts along the perivascular sheaths of pulmonary blood vessels, or rupture of subpleural bleb

KB27.4.title: Pneumoperitoneum, originating in the perinatal period, due to primary pulmonary air leak syndromes

KB28.title: Pulmonary haemorrhage originating in the perinatal period
KB28.definition: A condition characterised by bleeding from the lung which begins during the period of time around childbirth, especially the five months before and one month after birth.

KB28.0.title: Tracheobronchial haemorrhage originating in the perinatal period
KB28.0.definition: A condition characterised by bleeding from the trachea or bronchi which begins during the period of time around childbirth, especially the five months before and one month after birth.

KB28.1.title: Traumatic pulmonary haemorrhage originating in the perinatal period
KB28.1.definition: Pulmonary haemorrhage in neonate as a result of trauma, generally from a respiratory suction catheter following deep suctioning.

KB29.title: Chronic respiratory disease originating in the perinatal period
KB29.definition: A group of conditions associated with the respiratory system which begin during the period of time around childbirth, especially the five months before and one month after birth, and which lasts for at least 3 months.

KB29.0.title: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia originating in the perinatal period
KB29.0.definition: Chronic lung disease requiring treatment with oxygen for at least 28 days and with a spectrum of severity from mild to severe, that predominantly affects premature infants.

KB2A.title: Apnoea of newborn
KB2A.definition: Any condition characterised by suspension of external breathing in a newborn (premature or term) which is not classified elsewhere

KB2A.0.title: Central neonatal apnoea
KB2A.0.definition: Central apnoea is a cessation of airflow > 20 seconds with loss of all respiratory effort. It is due to immaturity of the brainstem to control respiration. It is found in many premature infants and generally resolves by 36 weeks of age.

KB2A.1.title: Obstructive neonatal apnoea
KB2A.1.definition: Apnoea that occurs secondary to diminished airway airflow from an obstruction in the airway from the nose and mouth, tongue, hypopharynx, epiglottis, vocal cords or subglottic region. This is characterised by initial increased work of breathing and rapid progression to cyanosis.

KB2A.2.title: Mixed neonatal apnoea
KB2A.2.definition: A combination of central apnoea and obstructive apnoea. Most apnoea of prematurity is of the mixed variety, and most often resolves by 36 weeks of age.

KB2A.3.title: Apnoea of newborn, due to neurologic injury

KB2B.title: Primary atelectasis of newborn
KB2B.definition: Failure of the lungs to expand after birth, as in stillborn infants or in liveborn infants who die before respiration is established

KB2C.title: Cyanotic attacks of newborn
KB2C.definition: Sudden attacks of cyanosis, lasting from a few moments up to half an hour, in an infant whose colour was previously normal, and whose colour returns to normal in atmospheric air after the attack

KB2D.title: Respiratory failure of newborn
KB2D.definition: Acute or chronic respiratory failure in a newborn. Neonates in acute respiratory failure require respiratory support.

KB2F.title: Congenital lung or lobar atelectasis
KB2F.definition: Collapsed lobe or lobes of the lung that is present at birth and is due to narrowing of the airway, kinking of the airway, compression from a mass in the airway or other congenital abnormality.

KB2G.title: Tracheal haemorrhage of newborn due to airway trauma
KB2G.definition: Trauma from suction catheters, endotracheal tubes, bronchoscopes that results in tracheal haemorrhage in the newborn.

KB2H.title: Acquired vocal cord paralysis in newborn
KB2H.definition: Acquired vocal cord paralysis may result from birth trauma, result of the extracorporeal membrane oxygenation cannulation, thoracic surgery, or some infections. Unilateral vocal cord paralysis is more common and the left vocal cord is most frequently involved.

KB2J.title: Airway obstruction in the neonate due to airway abnormality

KB2J.0.title: Hypotonia of hypopharynx in neonate
KB2J.0.definition: Poor muscle tone of the hypopharynx.

KB2J.2.title: Tracheo-bronchial malacia in neonate
KB2J.2.definition: Tracheomalacia is a condition characterised by flaccidity of the tracheal support cartilage causing weakness of the tracheobronchial tree and tracheal collapse.

KB2K.0.title: Acquired pulmonary cysts in newborn
KB2K.0.definition: Cysts occurring as a result of infection or trauma from mechanical ventilation resulting in pulmonary interstitial emphysema.

KB40.title: Neonatal cardiac failure
KB40.definition: Cardiac failure originating in the neonatal period

KB40.0.title: Neonatal cardiac failure due to pulmonary overperfusion
KB40.0.definition: Neonatal cardiac failure due to pulmonary overperfusion

KB40.1.title: Neonatal cardiac failure due to decreased left ventricular output

KB41.title: Cardiac arrhythmias in the neonate
KB41.definition: Abnormal electrical rhythm, both tachyarrhythmias and bradyarrhythmias, in neonate

KB42.title: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
KB42.definition: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn is a cardiopulmonary disorder characterised by systemic arterial hypoxemia secondary to pulmonary hypertension and extrapulmonary right-to-left shunting across the foramen ovale and ductus arteriosus.

KB44.title: Transient myocardial ischaemia of newborn
KB44.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by an imbalance between the oxygen supply and demand of the heart muscle (myocardium) in a newborn.

KB45.title: Neonatal hypertension
KB45.definition: Hypertension is defined by a systolic blood pressure in a neonate which is >95th percentile for age and sex on 3 separate occasions

KB46.title: Neonatal hypotension
KB46.definition: Mean Arterial Blood Pressure below gestational age in weeks (corresponds with 10th centile for birth weight and postnatal age 1) or below 30 mmHg as hypotension.

KB47.title: Benign or innocent cardiac murmurs in newborn
KB47.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by heart sounds that are produced as a result of turbulent blood flow that is sufficient to produce audible noise primarily due to physiologic conditions outside the heart, as opposed to structural defects in the heart itself in a newborn.

KB48.title: Patent arterial duct of prematurity
KB48.definition: Patent arterial duct associated with the child being born prior to completing 37 weeks of gestation, in the absence of ductal-dependent congenital heart disease.

KB60.title: Transitory disorders of carbohydrate metabolism specific to fetus or newborn
KB60.definition: A group of paediatric conditions in which there is a temporary disorder in a newborn or infant associated with abnormal chemical reactions in the body disrupting the process of getting or making energy from consumed carbohydrates.

KB60.0.title: Syndrome of infant of mother with gestational diabetes
KB60.0.definition: Describes the range of effects on the infant born to a woman with gestational diabetes (onset or first recognition of carbohydrate intolerance of variable severity in pregnancy). Common neonatal effects include macrosomia, intrauterine growth restriction, birth injuries, congenital anomalies, hypoglycaemia, respiratory distress, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

KB60.1.title: Syndrome of infant of a diabetic mother, type 1 or 2, nongestational, insulin dependent
KB60.1.definition: Describes the range of effects on the infant born to a woman with pregestational diabetes mellitus (type 1 or type 2). Common neonatal effects include macrosomia, intrauterine growth restriction, birth injuries, congenital anomalies, hypoglycaemia, respiratory distress, caudal regression syndrome and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

KB60.2.title: Neonatal diabetes mellitus
KB60.2.definition: Neonatal diabetes mellitus (NDM) is a monogenic form of diabetes that occurs in the first 6 months of life. It is a rare condition occurring in only one in 100,000 to 500,000 live births. Infants with NDM do not produce enough insulin, leading to an increase in blood glucose. NDM can be mistaken for the much more common type 1 diabetes, but type 1 diabetes usually occurs later than the first 6 months of life. In about half of those with NDM, the condition is lifelong and is called permanent neonatal diabetes mellitus (PNDM). In the rest of those with NDM, the condition is transient and disappears during infancy but can reappear later in life; this type of NDM is called transient neonatal diabetes mellitus (TNDM).

KB60.20.title: Transient neonatal diabetes mellitus
KB60.20.definition: Transient neonatal diabetes mellitus (TNDM) is a developmental disorder of insulin production that resolves postnatally within the first year of life. Intrauterine growth restriction is usually present. TNDM infants develop diabetes in the first few weeks of life but may go into remission in a few months, with possible relapse to a permanent diabetes state usually around adolescence or as adults. The pancreatic dysfunction in this condition may be maintained throughout life, with relapse initiated at times of metabolic stress such as puberty or pregnancy.

KB60.30.title: Neonatal hyperglycaemia due to insulin deficiency

KB60.31.title: Neonatal hyperglycaemia due to iatrogenic intravenous therapy

KB60.40.title: Transient hyperinsulinaemic neonatal hypoglycaemia
KB60.40.definition: This refers to transient above normal level of insulin in the blood, and an abnormally diminished content of glucose in the blood, of a newborn.

KB60.41.title: Transitory iatrogenic neonatal hypoglycaemia
KB60.41.definition: A condition associated with hypoglycemia as a result of therapeutic intervention. Often occurs with insulin therapy, but may also result from inadequate provision of glucose.

KB61.title: Transitory neonatal disorders of calcium or magnesium metabolism
KB61.definition: A group of paediatric conditions in which there is a temporary disorder in a newborn associated with abnormal chemical reactions in the body disrupting the normal processes of enzyme catalyzed reactions to utilize calcium and magnesium for other body functions.

KB61.0.title: Neonatal hypomagnesaemia
KB61.0.definition: Defined as serum magnesium levels less than 0.66 mmol/L (1.6 mg/L) in neonates. Symptoms usually do not develop until serum Magnesium (Mg) levels fall below 0.49 mmol/L (1.2 mg/L). This is usually transient but can cause symptoms similar to those of hypocalcaemia.

KB61.1.title: Neonatal tetany without calcium or magnesium deficiency
KB61.1.definition: Features of tetany (hyperexcitability, hyperreflexia, spasms and laryngospasm) not accompanied by low calcium or magnesium levels

KB61.2.title: Neonatal hypocalcaemia
KB61.2.definition: Hypocalcaemia is a common metabolic problem in newborns. In the neonate, hypocalcaemia is defined by birth weight (BW) categories. In infants with BW greater than 1500 g, hypocalcaemia is defined as a total serum calcium (Ca) concentration less than 8 mg/dL (2 mmol/L) or an ionized fraction of less than 4.4 mg/dL (1.1 mmol/L). In very low birth weight premature infants (BW<1500 g), hypocalcaemia is defined as a total serum Ca concentration less than 7 mg/dL (1.75 mmol/L) or an ionized fraction of less than 4 mg/dL (1 mmol/L). Aetiologies of early hypocalcaemia (occurs in the first two to three days after birth) include prematurity, maternal diabetes, birth asphyxia, and intrauterine growth. Causes of late hypocalcaemia (usually occurs at the end of the first week of life) include hypoparathyroidism and high phosphate intake. Most infants with hypocalcaemia are asymptomatic. If symptomatic, neuromuscular irritability is the most common sign with jitteriness and muscle jerking. Less common findings include seizures, and rarely laryngospasm, wheezing, or vomiting.

KB61.3.title: Neonatal osteopenia
KB61.3.definition: Metabolic bone disease is a common complication in very low birthweight (VLBW) preterm infants. The smallest, sickest infants are at greatest risk. Progressive osteopenia with demineralized bones and, occasionally, pathologic fractures may develop. The major cause is inadequate intake of calcium and phosphorus to meet the requirements for growth. Poor intake of vitamin D is an additional risk factor. Contributing factors include prolonged parenteral nutrition, vitamin D and calcium malabsorption, intake of unsupplemented human milk, immobilization, and urinary calcium losses from long-term diuretic use.

KB62.title: Transitory neonatal disorders of thyroid function
KB62.definition: A group of paediatric conditions in which there is a temporary disorder in a newborn or infant associated with the thyroid.

KB62.0.title: Transitory neonatal hyperthyroidism
KB62.0.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by a temporarily abnormally increased level of thyroid hormones (triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4)) in the blood of a newborn.

KB62.1.title: Other transitory neonatal disorders of thyroid function, not elsewhere classified
KB62.1.definition: Any other paediatric condition characterised by abnormal or absent function of the thyroid gland in a newborn.

KB62.2.title: Transient hyperthyrotropinaemia
KB62.2.definition: Transient hyperthyrotropinaemia is characterised by elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and normal thyroxine (FT4) levels with the elevated TSH levels eventually normalising.

KB62.3.title: Transient hypothyroxinaemia
KB62.3.definition: Transient hypothyroxinaemia is characterised by low thyroxine (T4, T3 and FT4) levels but normal level of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), and is seen in preterm infants, usually those born before 30 weeks of gestational age.

KB63.title: Certain specified transitory neonatal electrolyte or metabolic disturbances
KB63.definition: A group of paediatric conditions in which there is a temporary abnormality in the normal processes of enzyme catalyzed reactions within tissue cells (metabolism) or with the levels of minerals in the blood or other body fluids.

KB63.0.title: Late metabolic acidosis of newborn
KB63.0.definition: Mild to moderate metabolic acidosis occurring between 1 to 3 weeks of age in otherwise healthy premature infants fed cow's milk and accompanied by poor growth. This is thought to be due to excessive protein content of the milk.

KB63.1.title: Dehydration of newborn
KB63.1.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by excessive loss of body water in a newborn.

KB63.2.title: Disturbances of sodium balance of newborn
KB63.2.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by abnormally high or low levels of sodium in the blood in a newborn, when the normal range is defined as 135 to 150 mEq/L.

KB63.20.title: Hyponatremia of newborn
KB63.20.definition: Hyponatremia is defined as serum sodium less than 130 mmol/L

KB63.21.title: Hypernatremia of newborn
KB63.21.definition: Hypernatremia is defined as serum sodium greater than 145 mmol/L.

KB63.3.title: Disturbances of potassium balance of newborn
KB63.3.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by abnormally high or low levels of potassium in the blood in a newborn, when the normal range is defined as 3.5 to 5.5 mmol/L.

KB63.30.title: Hypokalaemia of newborn
KB63.30.definition: Hypokalaemia is defined as serum potassium less than 3.5 mmol/L.

KB63.31.title: Hyperkalaemia of newborn
KB63.31.definition: Hyperkalaemia is defined as serum potassium greater than 5.5 mmol/L.

KB63.4.title: Transitory tyrosinaemia of newborn
KB63.4.definition: Clinically asymptomatic elevated blood tyrosine level caused by late fetal maturation of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase, usually detected on newborn bloodspot screening. Most commonly seen in premature infants receiving milk formulae with high protein content. Generally considered benign and resolves by 4-6 weeks of age.

KB63.5.title: Metabolic bone disease of prematurity
KB63.5.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by bone abnormalities in a newborn due to abnormalities of minerals such as calcium, phosphorus, magnesium or vitamin D associated with the child being born prior to completing 37 weeks of gestation.

KB64.title: Transitory neonatal hypoparathyroidism
KB64.definition: Defined as hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphatemia and low serum parathyroid hormone that improves spontaneously but may last from weeks to months.

KB80.title: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease in newborn
