LD44.L1.title: Deletions of the short arm of chromosome 20

LD44.N0.title: CATCH 22 phenotype
LD44.N0.definition: Monosomy 22q11 (DiGeorge Velocardiofacial syndrome, DGS/VCF) syndrome is a chromosomal anomaly characterised by the association of several variable malformations: hypoplastic thymus and parathyroid glands, congenital conotruncal heart defects, a subtle but characteristic facial dysmorphism, cleft palate or velar insufficiency, and learning difficulties.

LD45.title: Uniparental disomies
LD45.definition: Any disease caused by the inheritance of two homologous copies of a chromosome from one parent, and none from the other parent. Confirmation is by observation of identical chromosomes pairs by genetic testing.

LD45.0.title: Uniparental disomies of maternal origin
LD45.0.definition: Any disease characterised by the inheritance of two homologous copies of a chromosome from the mother, and none from the father. Confirmation is by observation of identical chromosome pairs, and matching to a maternal chromosome, by genetic testing.

LD45.1.title: Uniparental disomies of paternal origin
LD45.1.definition: Any disease caused by the inheritance of two homologous copies of a chromosome from the father, and none from the mother. Confirmation is by observation of identical chromosome pairs, and matching to a paternal chromosome, by genetic testing.

LD47.title: Balanced rearrangements or structural rearrangements
LD47.definition: A condition caused by translocation or other structural rearrangement of genomic material between chromosomes demonstrating no net gain or loss of genomic material, in an individual displaying no phenotype. Confirmation is through observation of a balanced event by genetic testing.

LD47.0.title: Balanced translocation and insertion in normal individual
LD47.0.definition: A condition caused by translocation of genetic material between chromosomes with no net gain or loss of genetic material, in an individual demonstrating no abnormalities. Confirmation is through observation of a balanced translocation and insertion by genetic testing.

LD47.1.title: Chromosome inversion in normal individual
LD47.1.definition: Any disease caused by inversion of genetic material on a chromosome, in an individual demonstrating no abnormalities. Confirmation is through observation of a chromosomal inversion by genetic testing.

LD47.2.title: Balanced autosomal rearrangement in abnormal individual
LD47.2.definition: Any disease caused by alteration of autosome structure with no net gain or loss of genetic material, in an individual demonstrating abnormalities. Confirmation is through observation of a balanced chromosomal rearrangement by genetic testing.

LD47.3.title: Balanced sex or autosomal rearrangement in abnormal individual
LD47.3.definition: Any disease caused by alteration of chromosomal structure with no net gain or loss of genetic material, in an individual demonstrating abnormalities. Confirmation is through observation of a balanced chromosomal rearrangement by genetic testing.

LD47.4.title: Autosomal fragile site
LD47.4.definition: Any disease caused by presence of a fragile site on an autosome. These diseases may present as asymptomatic. Confirmation is through observation of a fragile site by genetic testing.

LD50.0.title: Turner syndrome
LD50.0.definition: Karyotype missing one X chromosome (45,X0 or 45,X0/46,XX mosaicism); gonads: ovaries (streak); phenotype female with short stature, amenorrhea (hypergonadotropic hypogonadism), absence of sexual development, webbed neck, low set ears, posterior hairline, widely-spaced nipples, short fourth metacarpals, and increased carrying angle at the elbow (cubitus valgus). Often associated with renal, cardiac and ocular abnormalities.

LD50.00.title: Karyotype 45, X
LD50.00.definition: A disease affecting females, caused by absence of one of the two X chromosomes. This disease may present with short stature, extra folds of skin on the neck, a low hairline at the back of the neck, puffiness or swelling of the hands and feet, skeletal abnormalities, ovarian hypofunction or premature ovarian failure, kidney problems, or heart defects. Confirmation is through observation of only one X chromosome by karyotyping.

LD50.01.title: Karyotype 46, X iso Xq
LD50.01.definition: A disease affecting females, caused by one of the two X chromosomes consisting of two q arms, which are structurally identical and contain the same genes. This disease may present with short stature, extra folds of skin on the neck, a low hairline at the back of the neck, puffiness or swelling of the hands and feet, skeletal abnormalities, ovarian hypofunction or premature ovarian failure, kidney problems, or heart defects. This disease may be differentiated from classical Turner Syndrome by a near complete lack of gonadal development, resulting in a lack of menstruation or breast development. Confirmation is through observation of an iso Xq chromosome by karyotyping.

LD50.02.title: Karyotype 46, X with abnormal sex chromosome, except iso Xq

LD50.03.title: Mosaicism, 45, X, 46, XX or XY
LD50.03.definition: A disease caused by embryonic fusion, or by the loss of one of the sex chromosomes from a cell early in embryonic development; Gonadal status: normal or variable abnormalities of sexual anatomy, maturation or function. Phenotype: normal, or abnormal sexual development.

LD50.04.title: Mosaicism, 45, X or other cell line with abnormal sex chromosome
LD50.04.definition: A disease caused by embryonic fusion or the structural mutation of a sex chromosome early in embryonic development, resulting in a subset of cells in the body having one normal copy of the X chromosome and one abnormal sex chromosome. This disease may present with short stature, sexual organ dysfunction, or may be asymptomatic.

LD50.1.title: Karyotype 47,XXX
LD50.1.definition: Trisomy X is a sex chromosome anomaly with a variable phenotype caused by the presence of an extra X chromosome in females (47,XXX instead of 46,XX). Most individuals are only mildly affected or asymptomatic, the most common physical features including tall stature, epicanthal folds, hypotonia and clinodactyly, with seizures, renal and genitourinary abnormalities, and premature ovarian failure being also associated findings.

LD50.2.title: Mosaicism, lines with various numbers of X chromosomes
LD50.2.definition: A disease caused by embryonic fusion or gain or loss of X chromosomes early in embryonic development, resulting in a subset of cells in the body having an abnormal number of X chromosomes. This disease may present with abnormal height, genitourinary abnormalities, or may be asymptomatic.

LD50.3.title: Klinefelter syndrome
LD50.3.definition: Klinefelter syndrome defines a group of chromosomal disorders in which there is at least one extra X chromosome compared with the normal 46,XY male karyotype. The effects on physical features and on physical and cognitive development increase with the number of extra X's, and each extra X is associated with an intelligence quotient (IQ) decrease of approximately 15-16 points, with language most affected, particularly expressive language skills.

LD50.30.title: Klinefelter syndrome with karyotype 47,XXY, regular
LD50.30.definition: Karyotype 47 XXY; gonads: testes (hypogonadism) small and firm with decreased spermatogenesis ; phenotype male with associated congenital abnormalities (decreased virilization due to decreased testosterone production, long arms and legs, short trunk, psychosocial problems).

LD50.31.title: Klinefelter syndrome, male with more than two X chromosomes
LD50.31.definition: A disease affecting males, caused by the presence of more than two X chromosomes in each cell. This disease is characterised by impaired sexual development, intellectual disability, distinctive facial features, skeletal abnormalities, poor coordination, and severe problems with speech. This disease may be differentiated from classic Klinefelter syndrome by increased severity of symptoms. Confirmation is through observation of more than two X chromosomes by karyotyping.

LD51.title: Structural anomalies of chromosome X, excluding Turner syndrome

LD52.0.title: Male with 46,XX karyotype
LD52.0.definition: A disease affecting males, characterised by hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, testosterone deficiency, and infertility. This condition may also present with hypospadias. This disease may be associated with abnormal crossing over of the sex chromosomes during meiosis in the father, resulting in the SRY gene being present on one or both copies of the X chromosome.

LD52.1.title: Male with double or multiple Y
LD52.1.definition: A condition affecting males, caused by the presence of supernumerary Y chromosomes. This condition is asymptomatic. Confirmation is through observation of supernumerary Y chromosomes by karyotyping.

LD54.title: Male with sex chromosome mosaicism
LD54.definition: Any disease affecting males, caused by embryonic fusion or gain or loss of a sex chromosome early in embryonic development, resulting in a subset of cells in the body having an abnormal number of sex chromosomes. These diseases may present with deficiencies in testosterone, abnormalities of sexual development, or infertility.

LD55.title: Fragile X chromosome
LD55.definition: Fragile X syndrome is a rare genetic disease associated with mild to severe intellectual deficit that may be associated with behavioural disorders and characteristic physical features.

LD56.title: Chimaera 46, XX, 46, XY
LD56.definition: A disease caused by XX and XY embryonic fusion or two distinct loss events of a sex chromosome from an XXY embryo early in development. This results in a subset of cells in the body having an XX karyotype, while other cells demonstrate an XY karyotype. This disease may present with abnormal genital development.

LD90.title: Conditions with disorders of intellectual development as a relevant clinical feature

LD90.0.title: Angelman syndrome
LD90.0.definition: Angelman syndrome is a neurogenetic disorder characterised by severe intellectual deficit and distinct facial dysmorphic (microcephaly, macrostomia, maxillary hypoplasia, prognathia), behavioural (outbursts of laughter with hand flapping, a happy demeanour, hyperactivity without aggression, short attention span, excitability and sleeping problems with decreased need to sleep, increased sensitivity to heat, attraction to and fascination with water), and neurological features (a puppet-like gait, ataxia and epileptic seizures).

LD90.1.title: Early-onset parkinsonism - intellectual deficit
LD90.1.definition: Early-onset parkinsonism with intellectual deficit is a basal ganglia disorder characterised by parkinsonian-type symptoms (postural changes, tremor, rigidity), megalencephaly and variable intellectual deficit. Other signs are frontal bossing, persistent frontal lobe reflexes, strabismus and seizures.

LD90.2.title: Pelizaeus-Merzbacher-like disease
LD90.2.definition: Pelizaeus-Merzbacher-like disease (PMLD) is an autosomal recessive leukodystrophy sharing identical clinical and radiological features as X-linked Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease (PMD).

LD90.3.title: Prader-Willi syndrome
LD90.3.definition: Prader-Willi syndrome is a rare genetic disorder characterised by hypothalamic-pituitary abnormalities with severe hypotonia during the neonatal period and first two years of life and the onset of hyperphagia with a risk of morbid obesity during infancy and adulthood, learning difficulties and behavioural problems or severe psychiatric problems.

LD90.4.title: Rett syndrome
LD90.4.definition: A condition in which apparently normal early development is followed by partial or complete loss of speech and of skills in locomotion and use of hands, together with deceleration in head growth, usually with an onset between seven and 24 months of age. Loss of purposive hand movements, hand-wringing stereotypies, and hyperventilation are characteristic. Social and play development are arrested but social interest tends to be maintained. Trunk ataxia and apraxia start to develop by age four years and choreoathetoid movements frequently follow. Severe mental retardation almost invariably results.

MA00.title: Symptom or complaint of the blood

MA01.title: Enlarged lymph nodes
MA01.definition: Enlarged lymph node is called lymphadenopathy which means the abnormal enlargement of lymph nodes.

MA10.0.title: Elevation of levels of transaminase or lactic acid dehydrogenase

MA10.1.title: Abnormal levels of other specified serum enzymes

MA10.2.title: Abnormal level of unspecified serum enzyme

MA11.title: Clinical findings of hormones in blood, blood-forming organs, or the immune system

MA12.title: Clinical findings of drugs, medicaments or biological substances in blood, blood-forming organs, or the immune system

MA12.0.title: Finding of opiate drug in blood

MA12.3.title: Finding of psychotropic drug in blood

MA12.4.title: Finding of steroid agent in blood

MA13.title: Clinical findings of substances chiefly nonmedicinal as to source in blood, blood-forming organs, or the immune system

MA13.0.title: Finding of abnormal level of heavy metals in blood

MA13.00.title: Abnormal level of lead in blood
MA13.00.definition: Abnormal level of lead in blood in those who have been exposed to lead and who require management.

MA14.title: Immunological findings in blood, blood-forming organs, or the immune system

MA14.0.title: Laboratory evidence of human immunodeficiency virus

MA15.title: Microbiological findings in blood, blood-forming organs, or the immune system

MA15.0.title: Bacteraemia
MA15.0.definition: The presence of bacteria in the blood. This can be detected, for example, by a positive blood culture.

MA16.title: Cytological findings in blood, blood-forming organs, or the immune system

MA17.title: Histological findings in blood, blood-forming organs, or the immune system

MA18.title: Certain clinical findings of blood chemistry

MA18.00.title: Abnormal glucose tolerance test
MA18.00.definition: Greater than normal levels of glucose found in laboratory examination of the blood to check how the body breaks down (metabolizes) blood sugar. Positive findings may indicate diabetes or Cushing diseases, among other things.

MA1A.title: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate or abnormality of plasma viscosity

MA50.title: Abnormal results of thyroid function studies

MA51.title: Abnormal results of other endocrine function studies

MA80.title: Speech or language disturbances
MA80.definition: Speech or language disturbances, not classified elsewhere include dysphasia and aphasia, dysarthria and anarthria, and other speech or language disturbances.

MA80.1.title: Dysphasia
MA80.1.definition: A cognitive disorder marked by an impaired ability to comprehend or express language in its written or spoken form. This condition is caused by diseases which affect the language areas of the dominant hemisphere. Clinical features are used to classify the various subtypes of this condition.

MA81.title: Speech dysfluency
MA81.definition: Speech dysfluency is characterised by the frequent or pervasive disruption of the rhythmic flow of speech that arises subsequent to the developmental period (i.e., adult onset) and is outside the limits of normal variation and results in reduced intelligibility and significantly affects communication. It can involve repetitions of sounds, syllables or words, prolongations, word breaks, blockage of production, excessive use of interjections, and rapid short bursts of speech.

MA82.title: Voice disturbances
MA82.definition: Voice disturbances include dysphonia, aphonia, hypernasality and hyponasality, and other voice disturbances.

MA82.0.title: Aphonia
MA82.0.definition: Aphonia is the inability to produce voice. It is considered more severe than dysphonia. Like dysphonia, aphonia can be caused by voice strain or overuse, injury, by structural laryngeal anomalies or by dystonic neurological disorders.

MA82.1.title: Dysphonia
MA82.1.definition: Difficulty and/or pain in phonation or speaking.

MA82.2.title: Nasality
MA82.2.definition: Nasality (or resonance) refers to the quality of the voice that is determined by the balance of sound vibration in the oral, nasal, and pharyngeal cavities during speech. Abnormal resonance can occur when there is obstruction in one of the cavities, causing hyponasality, or when there is velopharyngeal dysfunction, causing hypernasality. This category should only be assigned when hyponasality or hypernasality is outside the limits of normal variation and results in reduced intelligibility and significantly affects communication.

MB20.title: Symptoms, signs or clinical findings involving consciousness
MB20.definition: Symptoms, signs, and clinical findings indicative of a disturbance in the state or quality of awareness of oneself and the environment, alertness, or clarity of the wakeful state.

MB20.0.title: Stupor
MB20.0.definition: Total or nearly total lack of spontaneous movement and marked decrease in reactivity to environment.

MB20.1.title: Coma
MB20.1.definition: Acute state lasting more than one hour and usually less than a month. The comatose patient is unresponsive, lying with their eyes closed and cannot be aroused even by vigorous and noxious stimuli. Motor responses to noxious stimulation are limited to reflexive behaviour. Etiologies include but are not limited to traumatic, anoxic, infectious, neoplastic, vascular, inflammatory and metabolic brain injuries.

MB20.2.title: Clouding of consciousness
MB20.2.definition: An impairment in the clarity of consciousness characterised by impaired ability to comprehend aspects of the environment or the self in relation to the environment, inattention, and abnormalities in thought processes, comprehension. It is typically accompanied by subjective experience of mental clouding described as feeling ‘foggy’. Clouding of consciousness is a common form of cognitive disturbance in Delirium, but it is not synonymous with Delirium because Delirium includes additional diagnostic requirements.

MB21.title: Symptoms, signs or clinical findings involving cognition
MB21.definition: Symptoms, signs, and clinical findings indicative of a disturbance in mental abilities and processes related to attention, memory, judgment, reasoning, problem solving, decision making, or comprehension, or the integration of these functions.

MB21.0.title: Age-associated cognitive decline
MB21.0.definition: A normative (non-pathological) deterioration of higher cortical functions such as thinking, reasoning, comprehension, calculation, learning, language, and judgment.

MB21.1.title: Amnesia
MB21.1.definition: An inability to recall past experiences, especially where recall is to be expected.

MB21.10.title: Anterograde amnesia
MB21.10.definition: An inability to recall past experiences, especially where recall is to be expected, occurring after an event (psychological or physical) presumed to be responsible for the amnesia.

MB21.11.title: Retrograde amnesia
MB21.11.definition: An inability to recall past experiences, especially where recall is to be expected, preceding an event (psychological or physical) presumed to be responsible for the amnesia.

MB21.12.title: Transient global amnesia
MB21.12.definition: A time-limited episode (lasting up to two days) of short-term memory loss without other signs or symptoms of neurological impairment.

MB21.2.title: Anosognosia
MB21.2.definition: A lack of awareness or failure to recognize one's own illness, symptoms, or functional deficits, considered to be an aspect of the illness.

MB21.3.title: Confabulation
MB21.3.definition: The filling of memory gaps with fabricated, distorted, or misinterpreted memories about oneself or the world, without the conscious intention to deceive.

MB21.4.title: Disorientation
MB21.4.definition: Impairment in or loss of awareness of the position of the self in relation to place, time, situation, or other persons. In severe cases, the sense of personal identity may also be lost.

MB21.5.title: Distractibility
MB21.5.definition: Difficulty focusing on tasks; attention is easily diverted by extraneous stimuli.

MB21.6.title: Impaired abstract thinking
MB21.6.definition: The inability to use concepts and to make and understand generalizations, such as the identifying the properties or pattern shared by a variety of specific items or events.

MB21.7.title: Impaired executive functioning
MB21.7.definition: Impairment in higher-level cognitive abilities, such as planning, sequencing, concept formation, abstracting, and decision-making.

MB21.8.title: Impaired judgment
MB21.8.definition: Deficit in the capacity to make sound, reasoned, and responsible decisions.

MB21.9.title: Perseveration
MB21.9.definition: Persistent repetition of previously used words, phrases, or details that are not responsive to the demands of the situation.

MB21.A.title: Poor concentration
MB21.A.definition: Difficulty focusing attention and sustaining the mental energy necessary to accomplish a task or goal.

MB21.B.title: Racing thoughts
MB21.B.definition: Subjective perception of accelerated thought processes.

MB22.title: Symptoms or signs involving motivation or energy
MB22.definition: Symptoms and signs involving motivation (the process that initiates, guides, and maintains goal-oriented behaviours) or energy (the strength and vitality required for sustained physical or mental activity).

MB22.0.title: Avolition
MB22.0.definition: A general lack of drive, or lack of motivation to pursue meaningful goals (e.g., as evidenced by limited participation in work, school, or socializing with others).

MB22.1.title: Decreased libido
MB22.1.definition: Decreased sexual desire or sexual activity compared with the patient's usual levels of sexual interest and functioning.

MB22.2.title: Demoralization
MB22.2.definition: Loss of confidence in one's ability to cope, with associated feelings of helplessness, hopelessness, and discouragement.

MB22.3.title: Hopelessness
MB22.3.definition: Little or no belief in a positive future.

MB22.4.title: Increased energy
MB22.4.definition: Increased physical or mental resources for activity, typically characterised by increased capacity for work and greater efficiency in responding to stimuli.

MB22.5.title: Increased goal-directed activity
MB22.5.definition: Increased planning of and participation in multiple activities (e.g. sexual, occupational, political, religious), compared to the individual's typical level of activity.

MB22.6.title: Increased libido
MB22.6.definition: Increased sexual desire or sexual activity compared with the patient's usual levels of sexual interest and functioning.

MB22.7.title: Tiredness
MB22.7.definition: Feeling of reduced alertness and an accompanying decrease in mental acuity, in some cases resulting in an impulse or tendency to fall asleep.

MB23.title: Symptoms or signs involving appearance or behaviour

MB23.0.title: Aggressive behaviour
MB23.0.definition: Actions intended to threaten or hurt another person or to damage property that may be physical, verbal, or symbolic (e.g., acting against the other person's interests). Aggressive behaviour may be appropriate and self-protective, or inappropriate, hostile, and destructive.

MB23.1.title: Antisocial behaviour
MB23.1.definition: Behaviour in which the basic rights of others or major age-appropriate societal norms, rules, or laws, are violated.

MB23.2.title: Avoidance behaviour
MB23.2.definition: The act of keeping away from circumstances, situations, or stimuli that cause anxiety or other negative emotions in the individual.

MB23.3.title: Bradyphrenia
MB23.3.definition: Slowness of thoughts or fatigability of initiative

MB23.4.title: Compulsions
MB23.4.definition: Repetitive behaviours or rituals (e.g., washing, checking) or mental acts (e.g., repeating words silently) that the individual feels driven to perform in response to an obsession, according to rigid rules, or to achieve a sense of ‘completeness’.

MB23.5.title: Coprolalia
MB23.5.definition: Involuntary swearing or the involuntary utterance of obscene words or socially inappropriate and derogatory remarks, often in Tourette syndrome.

MB23.6.title: Disorganised behaviour
MB23.6.definition: Behaviour including posture, gait, and other activity that is unpredictable or not goal-directed (e.g., shouting at strangers on the street).

MB23.7.title: Disheveled appearance
MB23.7.definition: Untidy or unkempt appearance reflecting a lack of attention to one or more aspects of hygiene, grooming, or dress.

MB23.8.title: Disruptive behaviour
MB23.8.definition: Behaviour that causes disorder and turmoil in others or one's environment (e.g., angry outbursts, arguments, disobedience).

MB23.9.title: Echolalia
MB23.9.definition: The automatic repetition of vocalizations, words, or phrases uttered by another person, which may be immediate or delayed (e.g., repetition of phrases earlier heard on television), without meaningful communicative function. Echolalia is a common feature of communication abnormalities in Autism spectrum disorder, but may also occur in other Mental, behavioural or neurodevelopmental disorders and certain neurological conditions, among children with severe visual impairment, and occasionally in typically developing children. Echolalia does not include repetition as a normal feature of language acquisition in early childhood development.

MB23.A.title: Excessive crying of child, adolescent, or adult
MB23.A.definition: Episodes of crying for several hours a day for more than several days a week for several weeks in an otherwise healthy child, adolescent, or adult.

MB23.C.title: Increased sociability
MB23.C.definition: Decrease or loss of normal social inhibitions manifested in increased impulses to be with and talk to other people, including overfamiliarity, compared to the individual's typical level of activity.

MB23.D.title: Mutism
MB23.D.definition: A lack of verbal output that may be generalised or restricted to specific situations.

MB23.E.title: Non-suicidal self-injury
MB23.E.definition: Intentional self-inflicted injury to the body, most commonly cutting, scraping, burning, biting, or hitting, with the expectation that the injury will lead to only minor physical harm.

MB23.F.title: Odd or peculiar appearance
MB23.F.definition: Grooming, clothing, or other aspects of personal appearance that are eccentric, unusual, or peculiar, and inconsistent with cultural or subcultural norms.

MB23.G.title: Odd or peculiar behaviour
MB23.G.definition: Behaviour including posture and gait that is eccentric, unusual, or peculiar, and is inconsistent with cultural or subcultural norms.

MB23.H.title: Panic attack
MB23.H.definition: A discrete episode of intense fear or apprehension accompanied by the rapid and concurrent onset of a number of characteristic symptoms. These symptoms may include, but are not limited to, palpitations or increased heart rate, sweating, trembling, sensations of shortness of breath, feelings of choking, chest pain, nausea or abdominal distress, feelings of dizziness or lightheadedness, chills or hot flushes, tingling or lack of sensation in extremities (i.e., paresthesias), depersonalization or derealization, fear of losing control or going mad, and fear of imminent death. Panic attacks can appear out of the blue or can be triggered by particular situations.

MB23.J.title: Poor personal hygiene
MB23.J.definition: Unwillingness or inability to maintain a level of personal cleanliness that is in keeping with the standards of the person's culture, society, or setting, such as not washing or brushing one's teeth.

MB23.K.title: Poverty of speech
MB23.K.definition: A general lack of the unprompted content and elaboration normally seen in speech that is attributed to poverty of thought. It is one of the negative symptoms of Schizophrenia.

MB23.L.title: Pressured speech
MB23.L.definition: Speech in which the person feels undue pressure to get the words out. The person’s speech is usually rapid, loud, and emphatic and may be difficult or impossible to interrupt. Frequently, the person talks without any social stimulation and may continue to talk even though no one is listening.

MB23.M.title: Psychomotor agitation
MB23.M.definition: Excessive motor activity, usually manifested by purposeless behaviours such as fidgeting, shifting, fiddling, inability to sit or stand still, wringing of the hands, etc.

MB23.N.title: Psychomotor retardation
MB23.N.definition: A visible generalised slowing of movements and speech.

MB23.Q.title: Social withdrawal
MB23.Q.definition: Retreat from relationships and other social interactions

MB23.R.title: Suicide attempt
MB23.R.definition: A specific episode of self-harming behaviour undertaken with the conscious intention of ending one's life.

MB23.S.title: Suicidal behaviour
MB23.S.definition: Concrete actions, such as buying a gun or stockpiling medication, that are taken in preparation for fulfilling a wish to end one's life but that do not constitute an actual suicide attempt.

MB24.title: Symptoms or signs involving mood or affect
MB24.definition: Symptoms and signs involving the regulation and expression of emotions or feeling states.

MB24.0.title: Ambivalence
MB24.0.definition: Conflicting ideas, wishes, or feelings toward a person, thing or situation that are distressing and may create difficulties in making decisions.

MB24.1.title: Anger
MB24.1.definition: An emotional state related to one's psychological interpretation of having been threatened that may range in intensity from mild irritation to intense fury and rage.

MB24.2.title: Anhedonia
MB24.2.definition: Inability to experience pleasure from normally pleasurable activities.

MB24.3.title: Anxiety
MB24.3.definition: Apprehensiveness or anticipation of future danger or misfortune accompanied by a feeling of worry, distress, or somatic symptoms of tension. The focus of anticipated danger may be internal or external.

MB24.4.title: Apathy
MB24.4.definition: A reduction or lack of feeling, emotion, interest, or concern; a state of indifference.

MB24.5.title: Depressed mood
MB24.5.definition: Negative affective state characterised by low mood, sadness, emptiness, hopelessness, or dejection

MB24.6.title: Disturbance of affect
MB24.6.definition: A disturbance in the expression or outward manifestation of mood.

MB24.60.title: Constricted affect
MB24.60.definition: A marked reduction in the expressive range and intensity of affect, but less than is observed in Blunted affect.

MB24.61.title: Blunted affect
MB24.61.definition: A severe reduction in the expressive range and intensity of affect, but less than is observed in Flat affect.

MB24.62.title: Flat affect
MB24.62.definition: Absence or near absence of any sign of affective expression.

MB24.63.title: Labile affect
MB24.63.definition: Marked variability in emotional expression, with repeated, rapid, and abrupt shifts.

MB24.64.title: Inappropriate affect
MB24.64.definition: Affective expression that is discordant with the content of the person's speech or ideation, or incompatible with the demands of a particular situation.

MB24.7.title: Dysphoria
MB24.7.definition: An unpleasant mood state, which can include feelings of depression, anxiety, discontent, irritability, and unhappiness

MB24.8.title: Elevated mood
MB24.8.definition: A positive mood state typically characterised by increased energy and self-esteem which may be out of proportion to the individual's life circumstances.

MB24.9.title: Euphoria
MB24.9.definition: An exaggerated feeling of physical and emotional well-being and vitality.

MB24.A.title: Fear
MB24.A.definition: An emotional response to perceived imminent threat or danger associated with urges to flee or fight.

MB24.B.title: Feelings of guilt
MB24.B.definition: Remorse related to past events or one's past actions (or inaction), thoughts, or desires.

MB24.C.title: Irritability
MB24.C.definition: A mood state characterised by being easily annoyed and provoked to anger, out of proportion to the circumstances.

MB24.D.title: Leaden paralysis
MB24.D.definition: A feeling that one's arms or legs are as heavy as lead, associated with a form of depression that also commonly includes overeating and oversleeping.

MB24.E.title: Mental rumination
MB24.E.definition: Mental preoccupation with negative events, personal characteristics, or failures.

MB24.F.title: Restlessness
MB24.F.definition: A feeling of being unable to keep still.

MB24.G.title: Tantrum
MB24.G.definition: An emotional outburst, usually among children or those in emotional distress, that is typically characterised by stubbornness, crying, screaming, defiance, anger, a resistance to attempts at pacification, and in some cases hitting or other violent behaviour.

MB24.H.title: Worry
MB24.H.definition: Unpleasant thoughts that are difficult to control, related to anticipated potential negative events.

MB25.title: Symptoms or signs involving form of thought
MB25.definition: Symptoms and signs involving the logical sequence and coherence of thought, typically manifest in speech, including thought disorder (circumstantiality, tangentiality, disorganised thinking and incoherence), flight of ideas, neologisms, and thought blocking.

MB25.0.title: Symptoms or signs of thought disorder
MB25.0.definition: Disturbances in the associative thought process typically manifest in speech or writing that range from circumstantiality to incoherence. These may be indicative of Schizophrenia and other primary psychotic disorders but can also occur in other mental disorders (e.g., Delirium).

MB25.00.title: Circumstantiality
MB25.00.definition: A relatively mild disturbance in the associative thought process typically manifest in speech or writing characterised by delay in getting to the point because of the interpolation of unnecessary details and irrelevant parenthetical remarks.

MB25.01.title: Tangentiality
MB25.01.definition: A disturbance in the associative thought process typically manifest in speech in which the person tends to digress readily from the topic under discussion to other topics through associations without ever returning to the original topic.

MB25.02.title: Disorganised thinking
MB25.02.definition: A disturbance in the associative thought process typically manifested in speech in which the person shifts suddenly from one topic to another that is unrelated or minimally related to the first. The individual gives no indication of being aware of the disconnectedness or illogicality of their thinking.

MB25.03.title: Incoherence
MB25.03.definition: Speech or thinking that is so disorganised that it is essentially incomprehensible to others.

MB25.1.title: Flight of ideas
MB25.1.definition: A nearly continuous flow of thoughts, usually manifested in speech, with rapid changes from topic to topic that are often based on understandable associations, distracting stimuli, or plays on words. In severe cases, the changes may be so rapid that speech is disorganised and incoherent.

MB25.2.title: Neologisms
MB25.2.definition: The invention of new words that have meaning only to the person using them. May also include the use of existing words in ways that are inconsistent with their common meaning.

MB25.3.title: Thought blocking
MB25.3.definition: A phenomenon usually manifested by the person's speech being suddenly interrupted by silences, experienced as a quick and total emptying of the mind.

MB26.title: Symptoms or signs involving content of thought
MB26.definition: Symptoms and signs involving content of thought include delusions, experiences of influence, passivity, and control, grandiosity, homicidal ideation, identity disturbance, obsessions, overvalued ideas, paranoid ideation, referential thinking, suspiciousness, and suicidal ideation.

MB26.0.title: Delusion
MB26.0.definition: A belief that is demonstrably untrue or not shared by others, usually based on incorrect inference about external reality. The belief is firmly held with conviction and is not, or is only briefly, susceptible to modification by experience or evidence that contradicts it. The belief is not ordinarily accepted by other members or the person's culture or subculture (i.e., it is not an article of religious faith).

MB26.00.title: Bizarre delusion
MB26.00.definition: A delusion that involves a phenomenon that would be regarded as physically impossible within the person's cultural context.

MB26.01.title: Delusion of being controlled
MB26.01.definition: A delusion that involves an external force or person controlling one's feelings, impulses, thoughts, or behaviour.

MB26.02.title: Delusion of guilt
MB26.02.definition: A delusion involving exaggerated or inappropriate responsibility, need for punishment or retribution, or disproportionate consequences of one’s actions, such as that a minor error in the past will lead to disaster, that the person has committed a sin or horrible crime and should be punished severely, or that the person is responsible for a horrible outcome with which there can be no possible connection.

MB26.03.title: Delusion of reference
MB26.03.definition: A delusion that events, objects, or other people in the person's immediate environment have a particular and unusual personal significance, usually of a negative or pejorative nature.

MB26.04.title: Erotomanic delusion
MB26.04.definition: A delusion that another person, usually of higher status, is in love with the individual.

MB26.05.title: Grandiose delusion
MB26.05.definition: A delusion of inflated worth, power, knowledge, identity, or special relationship to a deity or famous person.

MB26.06.title: Jealous delusion
MB26.06.definition: A delusion that one's sexual partner is unfaithful.

MB26.07.title: Persecutory delusion
MB26.07.definition: A delusion in which the central theme is that one (or someone to whom one is close) is being attacked, mocked, harassed, cheated, conspired against, or persecuted.

MB26.08.title: Religious delusion
MB26.08.definition: A delusion involving religious or spiritual themes or subject matter that other members of the person's religious group do not accept as possible.

MB26.09.title: Somatic delusion
MB26.09.definition: A delusion involving the functioning or appearance of one’s body, including of having a serious disease.

MB26.0A.title: Nihilistic delusion
MB26.0A.definition: A delusion that the self, part of the self, part of the body, other persons, or the whole world has ceased to exist.

MB26.0B.title: Misidentification delusion
MB26.0B.definition: A delusion that people in one’s environment, which may include family members and loved ones, are imposters or actors or are otherwise not who they seem to be.

MB26.0C.title: Delusion of impoverishment
MB26.0C.definition: A delusional conviction that one is currently destitute or soon will be, or that one does not have the necessary financial resources to live on, in spite of evidence to the contrary.

MB26.1.title: Experiences of influence, passivity, and control
MB26.1.definition: The experience that one's feelings, impulses, thoughts, bodily functions, or behaviour are under the control of another person or other external force instead of under one's own control. These experiences may or may not be accompanied by a delusional belief that provides an explanation for the subjective experience.

MB26.10.title: Thought broadcasting
MB26.10.definition: The experience that one's thoughts are accessible by others so that others know what one is thinking.

MB26.11.title: Thought insertion
MB26.11.definition: The experience that certain thoughts are being placed in one's mind by others.

MB26.12.title: Thought withdrawal
MB26.12.definition: The experience that one's thoughts are being removed by an outside person or force.

MB26.2.title: Grandiosity
MB26.2.definition: Exaggerated self-esteem or an unrealistic belief in one's superiority, importance, capacities, or identity.

MB26.3.title: Homicidal ideation
MB26.3.definition: Thoughts, ideas, or ruminations about killing another person, which range from vague ideas of revenge to detailed and fully formulated plans but do not include actual homicidal attempts.

MB26.4.title: Identity disturbance
MB26.4.definition: Distortion or inconsistency in the sense or view of sameness and historical continuity of one's self.

MB26.5.title: Obsessions
MB26.5.definition: Repetitive and persistent thoughts (e.g., of contamination), images (e.g., of violent scenes), or impulses/urges (e.g., to stab someone) that are experienced as intrusive, unwanted, and are commonly associated with anxiety.

MB26.6.title: Overvalued ideas
MB26.6.definition: Unreasonable and sustained beliefs that are maintained with less than delusional intensity (i.e., the person is able to acknowledge the possibility that the belief may not be true). An alternative use of this term is to refer to conventional or plausible thoughts (e.g., religious concepts, political ideas, or excessively idealistic beliefs) that are held with such a level of intensity so that the person's life is taken up by them.

MB26.7.title: Paranoid ideation
MB26.7.definition: Ideation, not held with delusional intensity, involving suspiciousness or beliefs of being harassed, persecuted, or unfairly treated by others.

MB26.8.title: Referential thinking
MB26.8.definition: Ideation, not held with delusional intensity, that random or coincidental events are of particular and unusual significance to the person.

MB26.9.title: Suspiciousness
MB26.9.definition: The behaviour of others is viewed with anxiety, mistrust, or hostility and perceived as potentially threatening.

MB26.A.title: Suicidal ideation
MB26.A.definition: Thoughts, ideas, or ruminations about the possibility of ending one's life, ranging from thinking that one would be better off dead to formulation of elaborate plans.

MB27.title: Symptoms or signs involving perceptual disturbance
MB27.definition: Symptoms and signs involving a disruption in sensory perception, including depersonalization, derealization, and hallucinations in any modality.

MB27.0.title: Depersonalisation
MB27.0.definition: Experiencing the self as strange or unreal, or feeling detached from, or as though one were an outside observer of, one’s thoughts, feelings, sensations, body, or actions. Depersonalization may take the form of emotional and/or physical numbing, a sense of watching oneself from a distance or ‘being in a play’, or perceptual alterations (e.g., a distorted sense of time).

MB27.1.title: Derealisation
MB27.1.definition: Experiencing other persons, objects, or the world as strange or unreal (e.g., dreamlike, distant, foggy, lifeless, colourless, or visually distorted) or feeling detached from one’s surroundings.

MB27.2.title: Hallucinations
MB27.2.definition: Sensory perceptions of any modality occurring in the absence of the appropriate (external) stimulus. The person may or may not have insight into the unreal nature of the perception.

MB27.20.title: Auditory hallucinations
MB27.20.definition: Hallucinations involving the perception of sound, most frequently of voices but sometimes of clicks or other noises, that are not restricted to the period of awakening or the onset of sleep.

MB27.21.title: Gustatory hallucinations
MB27.21.definition: Hallucinations of taste in the absence of an actual external stimulus.

MB27.22.title: Hypnopompic hallucinations
MB27.22.definition: Hallucinations that occur during the period of awakening, most commonly of the visual, tactile or auditory modality.

MB27.23.title: Hypnagogic hallucinations
MB27.23.definition: Hallucinations that occur at the onset of sleep, most commonly of the visual, tactile or auditory modality.

MB27.24.title: Olfactory hallucinations
MB27.24.definition: Hallucinations involving the perception of odour (e.g., of burning rubber, decaying fish, orange peel) in the absence of an actual external stimulus.

MB27.25.title: Somatic hallucinations
MB27.25.definition: Hallucinations involving the perception of an unusual physical state or event within the body, such as an electrical impulse running down one's arms or an object inside one's chest.

MB27.26.title: Tactile hallucinations
MB27.26.definition: Hallucinations involving the perception of being touched (e.g., feeling like bugs are crawling on the skin, pins being stuck into one's finger) that are not restricted to the period of awakening or the onset of sleep.

MB27.27.title: Visual hallucinations
MB27.27.definition: Hallucinations involving sight in the absence of an actual visual stimulus that are not restricted to the period of awakening or the onset of sleep. Visual hallucinations may involve formed images, such as of people, or of unformed images, such as flashes of light. Visual hallucinations must be distinguished from illusions, which are visual misperceptions of real external stimuli.

MB27.3.title: Disturbance of body image
MB27.3.definition: Excessively negative, distorted, or inaccurate perception of one's own body or parts of it.

MB27.4.title: Illusions
MB27.4.definition: A misinterpretation of a true sensation (e.g., hearing voices in the sound of running water, the perception of figures in shadows).

MB28.title: Symptoms or signs related to personality features
MB28.definition: Symptoms and signs involving the characteristics or qualities possessed by a person that uniquely influence his or her cognition, motivations, and behaviours in various situations.

MB28.0.title: Attention seeking
MB28.0.definition: A tendency to engage in behaviour designed to attract notice and to make oneself the focus of others’ attention.

MB28.1.title: Callousness
MB28.1.definition: Lack of concern for the feelings or problems of others; a lack of guilt or remorse about the negative or harmful effects of one's actions on others.

MB28.2.title: Eccentricity
MB28.2.definition: A tendency toward appearance or behaviour that is odd, unusual, peculiar, or unconventional, and is inconsistent with cultural or subcultural norms.

MB28.3.title: Entitlement
MB28.3.definition: The belief that one is inherently deserving of privileges or special treatment.

MB28.4.title: Hostility
MB28.4.definition: A tendency to experience persistent or frequent angry feelings, especially in response to minor slights and insults, and to adopt an unfriendly or threatening attitude in interactions with others.

MB28.5.title: Impulsivity
MB28.5.definition: A tendency to act on the spur of the moment in response to immediate stimuli, characterised by lack of deliberation and failure to consider risks and consequences before acting. Impulsivity may reflect a desire for immediate rewards or an inability to delay gratification.

MB28.6.title: Indecisiveness
MB28.6.definition: A tendency to have difficulty making decisions or committing to a course of action.

MB28.7.title: Irresponsibility
MB28.7.definition: A pattern of disregard for and failure to honour obligations or commitments; a lack of respect for and follow-through on agreements or promises; carelessness with others' property.

MB28.8.title: Low frustration tolerance
MB28.8.definition: Diminished ability to regulate one's emotions and behaviour in response to frustrating circumstances.

MB28.A.title: Negative affectivity
MB28.A.definition: A tendency to experience a broad range of distressing emotions, e.g. anxiety, anger irritability, depression, and other negative emotional states, often in response to even relatively minor actual or perceived stressors.

MB28.B.title: Negativism
MB28.B.definition: A tendency to oppose or resist suggestions or advice, or to resist stubbornly for no apparent reason.

MB28.C.title: Perfectionism
MB28.C.definition: An inclination to demand flawlessness of oneself or others and setting excessively high standards.

MB28.D.title: Pessimism
MB28.D.definition: An inclination to emphasize adverse aspects, conditions, and possibilities, or to expect the worst possible outcome.

MB28.E.title: Recklessness
MB28.E.definition: A tendency to engage in behaviour that potentially endangers a person's physical health, safety, or life.

MB28.F.title: Sensation seeking
MB28.F.definition: An inclination to search for experiences and feelings that are varied, novel, complex, and intense.

MB28.G.title: Stubbornness
MB28.G.definition: A steadfast adherence to an opinion, purpose, or course of action in spite of reason, arguments, or persuasion.

MB28.H.title: Submissiveness
MB28.H.definition: A tendency to adapt one’s behaviour to the actual or perceived interests and desires of others even when doing so is antithetical to one’s own interests, needs, or desires.

MB29.title: Symptoms or signs involving eating and related behaviour
MB29.definition: Symptoms and signs related to disturbances in the regulation or form of eating behaviour that are not developmentally appropriate or culturally sanctioned, including avoidant or restrictive eating, binge eating, decreased appetite, eating of non-nutritive substances, increased appetite, purging behaviour, and rumination-regurgitation.

MB29.0.title: Avoidant or restrictive eating
MB29.0.definition: Acceptance of only a limited diet, which may be defined in terms of a specific dietary composition or sensory features of food, that is inconsistent with cultural or subcultural norms.

MB29.1.title: Binge eating
MB29.1.definition: An episode in which an individual eats notably more than usual and feels that she or he is unable to stop or limit the amount or type of food eaten.

MB29.2.title: Eating of non-nutritive substances
MB29.2.definition: Consumption of non-food objects and materials (e.g., clay, soil, chalk, plaster, plastic, metal and paper) or raw food ingredients (e.g., large quantities of salt or corn flour).

MB29.3.title: Purging behaviour
MB29.3.definition: Behaviour aimed at the removal of ingested food from the body with the specific intention to lose weight or prevent weight gain (e.g., self-induced vomiting, laxative abuse, or the use of enemas).

MB29.4.title: Rumination-regurgitation
MB29.4.definition: Rechewing of previously swallowed food that has been brought back to the mouth through regurgitation, which may then be reswallowed or spat out.

MB2A.title: Symptoms or signs involving elimination
MB2A.definition: Symptoms and signs involving the behavioural components of defecation (soiling, faecal elimination) and urination.

MB2A.0.title: Soiling
MB2A.0.definition: The passage of faeces in clothing, bed, or other inappropriate places in an individual who has reached a developmental age where faecal continence is ordinarily expected.

MB2A.1.title: Wetting
MB2A.1.definition: The voiding of urine into clothes or bed, which may occur during the day or night in an individual who has reached a developmental age where urinary continence is ordinarily expected.

MB40.1.title: Allodynia
MB40.1.definition: Pain due to a normally non-painful stimulus

MB40.3.title: Anaesthesia of skin
MB40.3.definition: Partial or complete loss of sensation affecting the skin, most commonly affecting a circumscribed area and resulting from sensory nerve damage as from injury or leprosy.

MB40.4.title: Tingling fingers or feet or toes

MB40.5.title: Hyperaesthesia
MB40.5.definition: Increased sensibility to stimuli of sense

MB41.title: Disturbances of smell or taste
MB41.definition: Disturbances of smell or taste include anosmia, parosmia, parageusia, and other disturbances of smell or taste.

MB41.2.title: Dysgeusia
MB41.2.definition: A disorder characterised by an alteration of the sense of taste

MB43.title: Dyssomnia
MB43.definition: Difficulties to fall asleep, or to remain sleeping

MB44.title: Abnormalities of gait or mobility
MB44.definition: Abnormalities of gait or mobility include ataxic gait, paralytic gait, difficulty in walking, immobility, and other abnormalities of gait or mobility.

MB44.1.title: Paralytic gait
MB44.1.definition: A collection of gait abnormalities due to affected motor control, sensory feedback, and muscle strength.

MB45.title: Lack of coordination
MB45.definition: Other lack of coordination is a lack of coordination other than abnormal involuntary movements and abnormalities of gait and mobility.

MB45.1.title: Automatism
MB45.1.definition: Repetitive unconscious gestures such as lip smacking, chewing or swallowing

MB45.4.title: Intention tremor
MB45.4.definition: Cerebellar tremor characterised by a broad course and low frequency

MB46.title: Abnormal involuntary movements
MB46.definition: Abnormal involuntary movements include abnormal head movements, tremor, cramp, spasm, fasciculation, and other abnormal involuntary movements

MB46.3.title: Drop attack
MB46.3.definition: A sudden spontaneous fall while standing and recovery within seconds or minutes

MB47.2.title: Clonus
MB47.2.definition: A series of involuntary muscle contractions and relaxations

MB47.4.title: Dystonia
MB47.4.definition: Sustained muscle contraction, involuntary movements that can lead to fixed abnormal postures

MB47.7.title: Muscle fibrillation
MB47.7.definition: An involuntary muscle contraction and relaxation in a muscle fiber

MB47.9.title: Myotonia
MB47.9.definition: Slow relaxation of the muscles after voluntary contraction

MB47.A.title: Ophthalmoparesis
MB47.A.definition: Paresis of one or more extraocular muscles

MB47.B.title: Opisthotonos
MB47.B.definition: Arching position of the body due spasm of the axial muscles along the spinal column

MB48.title: Dizziness or giddiness
MB48.definition: Terms which may refer to a sense of spatial disorientation, motion of the environment, or lightheadedness. Dizziness is a general feeling of being off-balance. Giddiness is the feeling that you or your surroundings are moving or spinning.

MB48.00.title: Vertigo of central origin
MB48.00.definition: Central vertigo is usually a result of an abnormal processing of the vestibular sensory input by the central nervous system due to either a disruption of central integrators (i.e. brain stem, cerebellum) or a sensory information mismatch (i.e. from the cortex). Lesions that affect the vestibular nerve or root entry zone (i.e. cerebellopontine angle [CPA] lesions) result in imbalance by affecting primary vestibular sensory information

MB49.title: Aura
MB49.definition: Reversible visual and/or sensory symptoms prior to a seizure (few seconds) or migraine with aura (20 minutes)

MB4B.0.title: Dyslexia or alexia
MB4B.0.definition: Dyslexia and alexia refer to the loss, usually in adulthood, of a previous ability to read fluently and to accurately comprehend written material that is inconsistent with general level of intellectual functioning and is acquired after the developmental period in individuals who had previously attained these skills, such as due to a stroke or other brain injury.

MB4B.1.title: Agnosia
MB4B.1.definition: Agnosia refers to the inability to recognize objects, shapes, people, sounds, or smells, which occurs despite otherwise normal functioning of the specific sense and is not accounted for by memory impairment.

MB4B.2.title: Acalculia
MB4B.2.definition: Acalculia refers to the loss, usually in adulthood, of a previous ability to perform simple mathematical calculations that is inconsistent with general level of intellectual functioning and is acquired after the developmental period in individuals who had previously attained these skills, such as due to a stroke or other brain injury.

MB4B.3.title: Agraphia
MB4B.3.definition: Agraphia refers to the loss, usually in adulthood, of a previous ability to write that is inconsistent with general level of intellectual functioning and is acquired after the developmental period in individuals who had previously attained these skills, such as due to a stroke or other brain injury.

MB4B.4.title: Anomia
MB4B.4.definition: Acquired difficulty in retrieving previously used vocabulary, particularly nouns and verbs.

MB4B.5.title: Dyscalculia
MB4B.5.definition: Dyscalculia refers to acquired difficulty with performing simple mathematical calculations that is inconsistent with general level of intellectual functioning, with onset after the developmental period in individuals who had previously attained these skills, such as due to a stroke or other brain injury.

MB4C.title: Gerstmann syndrome
MB4C.definition: Gerstmann syndrome is a very rare neurological disorder characterised by the specific association of acalculia, finger agnosia, left-right disorientation, and agraphia, which is supposed to be secondary to a focal subcortical white matter damage in the parietal lobe.

MB4D.title: Headache, not elsewhere classified
MB4D.definition: Headache with characteristic features suggesting that it is a unique diagnostic entity, a finding or complaint, but not fulfilling criteria for any of the headache disorders classified elsewhere.

MB50.0.title: Flaccid tetraplegia
MB50.0.definition: This is a severe or complete loss of motor function in all four limbs with limp and relaxed muscles.

MB50.1.title: Spastic tetraplegia
MB50.1.definition: This is a severe or complete loss of motor function in all four limbs with involuntary contractions.

MB51.title: Diplegia of upper extremities
MB51.definition: This is a loss of motor control in both arms.

MB53.title: Hemiplegia
MB53.definition: This is a severe or complete loss of motor function on one side of the body.

MB53.1.title: Flaccid hemiplegia
MB53.1.definition: This is a severe or complete loss of motor function on one side of the body with limp and relaxed muscles.

MB53.2.title: Spastic hemiplegia
MB53.2.definition: This is a severe or complete loss of motor function on one side of the body with involuntary contractions.

MB54.title: Monoplegia of upper extremity
MB54.definition: This is a loss of motor control in one arm.

MB55.title: Monoplegia of lower extremity
MB55.definition: This is a loss of motor control in one leg.

MB57.title: Functional level of injury of spinal cord

MB57.0.title: Functional level of injury of cervical spinal cord

MB57.1.title: Functional level of injury of thoracic spinal cord

MB57.2.title: Functional level of injury of lumbar spinal cord

MB57.3.title: Functional level of injury of spinal cord, sacrum

MB70.0.title: Abnormal level of enzymes in cerebrospinal fluid

MB70.1.title: Abnormal level of hormones in cerebrospinal fluid

MB70.2.title: Abnormal level of drugs, medicaments or biological substances in cerebrospinal fluid

MB70.3.title: Abnormal level of substances chiefly nonmedicinal as to source in cerebrospinal fluid

MB70.4.title: Abnormal immunological findings in cerebrospinal fluid

MB70.5.title: Abnormal microbiological findings in cerebrospinal fluid

MB70.6.title: Abnormal cytological findings in cerebrospinal fluid

MB70.7.title: Abnormal histological findings in cerebrospinal fluid

MB70.8.title: Other abnormal findings in cerebrospinal fluid

MB71.title: Clinical findings on diagnostic imaging of central nervous system
MB71.definition: Clinical findings on diagnostic imaging of central nervous system is findings on diagnostic imaging of the brain or the spinal cord which don't appear in normal status of the body. Diagnostic imaging refers to technologies that doctors use to look inside body for clues about a medical condition. X-rays, CT scans, nuclear medicine scans, MRI scans and ultrasound are all types of diagnostic imaging.

MB72.title: Results of function studies of the nervous system

MC13.title: Epiphora
MC13.definition: This is overflow of tears onto the face. A clinical sign or condition that constitutes insufficient tear film drainage from the eyes in that tears will drain down the face rather than through the nasolacrimal system.

MC1A.title: Visual floaters
MC1A.definition: Floaters are dark spots or shapes that seem to float in front of the retinal image.

MC1B.title: Symptom or complaint of the eyelid

MC1D.title: Symptom or complaint of contact lens

MC20.title: Clinical findings of the visual system

MC20.0.title: Staphyloma
MC20.0.definition: This is an abnormal protrusion of the uveal tissue through a weak point in the eyeball. The protrusion is generally black in colour, due to the inner layers of the eye. It occurs due to weakening of outer layer of eye (cornea or sclera) by an inflammatory or degenerative condition. It may be of 5 types, depending on the location on the eye ball (bulbus oculi).

MC20.2.title: Hypopyon
MC20.2.definition: Hypopyon is inflammatory cells in the anterior chamber of eye. It is a leukocytic exudate, seen in the anterior chamber, usually accompanied by redness of the conjunctiva and the underlying episclera. It is a sign of inflammation of the anterior uvea and iris, i.e. iritis, which is a form of anterior uveitis. The exudate settles at the bottom due to gravity.

MC21.1.title: Normal electroretinogram
MC21.1.definition: An Electro-Retinogram records retinal action potentials in response to various visual stimuli.

MC41.title: Tinnitus
MC41.definition: A nonspecific symptom of hearing disorder characterised by the sensation of buzzing, ringing, clicking, pulsations, and other noises in the ear in the absence of appropriate corresponding external stimuli and in the absence of what the examiner can hear with a stethoscope.

MC80.title: Abnormal blood-pressure reading, without diagnosis of hypertension or hypotension
MC80.definition: Abnormal blood-pressure reading, without diagnosis of hypertension or hypotension is a reading of blood pressure which is higher than normal blood pressure or lower than normal blood pressure, without a conclusive diagnosis.

MC80.0.title: Elevated blood-pressure reading, without diagnosis of hypertension

MC80.00.title: White coat hypertension
MC80.00.definition: Persistently elevated office blood pressure readings with persistently normal out-of-the-office readings.

MC80.01.title: Combined diastolic and systolic elevated blood pressure reading without diagnosis of hypertension

MC80.02.title: Diastolic elevated blood pressure reading without diagnosis of hypertension

MC80.03.title: Systolic elevated blood pressure reading without diagnosis of hypertension

MC81.title: Abnormalities of heart beat
MC81.definition: Abnormalities of heart beat is arrhythmia which is any disorder of the heart rate or rhythm. It means that the heart beats too quickly, too slowly or with an irregular pattern.

MC81.4.title: Pulseless electrical activity, not elsewhere classified

MC82.title: Cardiac arrest
MC82.definition: A sudden, sometimes temporary, cessation of heart function resulting in hemodynamic collapse.

MC82.0.title: Ventricular tachycardia and fibrillation cardiac arrest
MC82.0.definition: Discoordinated or rapid ventricular depolarization resulting in hemodynamic collapse.

MC82.1.title: Bradycardic cardiac arrest
MC82.1.definition: Slow escape rhythm associated with hemodynamic collapse.

MC82.2.title: Asystolic cardiac arrest
MC82.2.definition: Absence of electrical activity of the heart resulting in hemodynamic collapse.

MC82.3.title: Cardiac arrest with pulseless electrical activity
MC82.3.definition: Electrical activation of the heart without mechanical activation resulting in hemodynamic collapse.

MC83.title: Cardiac murmurs or other cardiac sounds
MC83.definition: Cardiac murmurs are blowing, whooshing, or rasping sounds heard during a heartbeat. Other cardiac sounds are sounds heard from heart other than cardiac murmurs.

MC85.title: Gangrene
MC85.definition: Gangrene, not elsewhere classified is the death of tissues in the body which happens when a part of the body loses its blood supply.

MC90.title: Clinical findings on diagnostic imaging of heart or coronary circulation

MC91.title: Results of function studies of the circulatory system

MD10.title: Abnormal sputum
MD10.definition: This category includes the abnormalities of quantity, colour and odor in sputum which may suggest an aetiology. Patients with chronic bronchitis typically expectorate small quantities of mucoid yellow material. A foul or fetid odor should suggest infection from anaerobic organisms, usually in cases of lung abscess. Occasionally, greatly excessive amounts of sputum or "bronchorrhoea" is associated with bronchioloalveolar carcinoma.

MD11.title: Abnormalities of breathing
MD11.definition: Abnormalities of breathing includes dyspnoea, stridor, wheezing, periodic breathing, hyperventilation, mouth breathing, hiccough, sneezing, and other abnormalities of breathing.

MD11.1.title: Asphyxia
MD11.1.definition: Asphyxia is a life-threatening condition in which oxygen is prevented from reaching the tissues by obstruction of or damage to any part of the respiratory system. More generally the term indicates all the conditions generating impaired or impeded breathing.

MD11.2.title: Ataxic breathing
MD11.2.definition: An irregular breathing pattern that usually progresses to complete apnoea.

MD11.4.title: Sleep related Cheyne-Stokes respiration
MD11.4.definition: Periodic breathing, a variant of Cheyne-Stokes respiration, is characterised by regular, recurrent cycles of changing tidal volumes in which the lowest tidal volume is less than half the maximal tidal volume in that cycle. It is the most frequent abnormal respiratory pattern directly related to stroke rather than underlying systemic disease, occurring in approximately 25 percent of patients. Periodic breathing may be more common among patients with subarachnoid haemorrhage.

MD11.5.title: Dyspnoea
MD11.5.definition: Dyspnoea is used to describe perceptions of difficulty or distress related to breathing and is recognised as symptomatic of disease when it occurs under inappropriate circumstances. Dyspnoea is a presenting complaint of patients with a wide variety of medical diseases by multiple mechanisms. Dyspnoea is considered acute when it lasts from hours up to 3 weeks, subacute from 3 weeks up to 8 weeks, and chronic dyspnoea lasts more than 8 weeks.

MD11.6.title: Hiccough
MD11.6.definition: Hiccough are repeated involuntary spasms of the diaphragm followed by sudden closure of the glottis, which checks the inflow of air and causes the characteristic sound. Transient episodes are very common. Persistent (> 2 days) and intractable (> 1 mo) Hiccough are uncommon but quite distressing.

MD11.7.title: Hyperventilation
MD11.7.definition: Hyperventilation refers to an increase in the rate of alveolar ventilation that is excessive for the rate of metabolic carbon dioxide production, resulting in a decrease in arterial PCO2 to below the normal range of 37 to 43 mm Hg. Hyperventilation should be distinguished from tachypnoea, an increase in respiratory frequency, and from hyperpnea, an increase in minute volume of ventilation.

MD11.8.title: Mouth breathing
MD11.8.definition: Breathing through mouth. Nasal obstruction may also necessitate mouth breathing, which itself can precipitate obstructive apnoea. Breathing through the mouth may also increase risk for OSA [obstructive sleep apnoea] by its effect on the tongue. The tongue forms the anterior wall of the oropharynx; both the supine posture and opening of the mouth tend to displace it posteriorly and encourage airway closure.

MD11.80.title: Stertor
MD11.80.definition: Stertor is a heavy snoring or gasping sound on inspiration occurring in coma or deep sleep that may be caused by partial obstruction of airway, choanal stenosis, enlarged tonsils and/or adenoids, and redundant upper airway tissues.

MD11.A.title: Sneezing
MD11.A.definition: Sneezing is one of the most fundamental airway reflexes, which is characterised by a deep preparatory inspiration followed by an abrupt increase in subglottic pressure reflecting a forceful, active expiration rather similar to coughing. Chemical or physical stimuli to the nasal mucosa may initiate potent respiratory and cardiovascular reflexes via stimulation of trigeminal nerves. Mild stimuli result in sneezing and nasal hypersecretion. These reflex responses protect the lower airways from inhalation of physical and chemical irritants.

MD11.B.title: Stridor
MD11.B.definition: Stridor or a low-pitched, focal inspiratory wheeze usually heard over the neck is a manifestation of upper airway obstruction and should result in an expedited evaluation of the patient as it can precede complete upper airway obstruction and respiratory failure.

MD11.C.title: Wheezing
MD11.C.definition: Continuous adventitious sounds that are high-pitched are called wheezes. Wheezes originate in airways narrowed by spasm, thickening of the mucosa, or luminal obstruction.

MD12.title: Cough
MD12.definition: Cough is an important natural defensive mechanism and protective reflex for clearing the upper and lower airways of excessive secretions such as mucus and inhaled particles. Cough is a common symptom of most respiratory disorders and may be indicative of trivial to very serious airway or lung pathology.

MD21.title: Haemorrhage from throat
MD21.definition: Haemorrhage from throat is the bleeding from throat. Throat is a tube that carries food to oesophagus and air to windpipe and larynx.

MD22.title: Haemoptysis
MD22.definition: Expectoration or spitting of blood originating from any part of the respiratory tract, usually from haemorrhage in the lung parenchyma and the bronchial arteries.

MD23.title: Haemorrhage from other sites in respiratory passages

MD24.title: Acute idiopathic pulmonary haemorrhage in infants over 28 days of age

MD30.title: Pain in throat or chest
MD30.definition: Pain in throat or chest means having pain sensation in throat or chest. Throat pain is a common ailment characterized by scratchiness, or irritation in the throat. It is frequently a symptom of an infection, but it can be due to many other conditions. Chest pain is any sort of pain felt in your chest area — from your shoulders to the bottom of your ribs. Chest pain can be a symptom of many different conditions, some of which are more serious than others.

MD30.0.title: Chest pain on breathing
MD30.0.definition: Pleuritic chest pain is a type of pain that is caused by problems with the thin layers of tissue that surround the lungs (called the “pleura”). This type of pain feels like a sharp, stabbing chest pain, and it gets worse when you breathe in. Pleuritic chest pain can be caused by the following problems: pneumothorax, pleural effusion, pleuritis, empyema, pericarditis.

MD31.title: Pleurisy
MD31.definition: Pleurisy or Pleuritis is the medical term for inflammation of the pleura. The most common cause of pleuritis is infection, but it can also be caused by lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, and certain medicines. Pleurisy or pleuritis usually accumulates exudative pleural effusions.

MD36.0.title: Pain in throat
MD36.0.definition: Pain in throat means having pain sensation in throat. Throat is a tube that carries food to oesophagus and air to windpipe and larynx.

MD41.title: Clinical findings on diagnostic imaging of lung
MD41.definition: Clinical findings on diagnostic imaging of lung is findings on diagnostic imaging of the lung which don't appear in normal status of the body. Diagnostic imaging refers to technologies that doctors use to look inside body for clues about a medical condition. X-rays, CT scans, nuclear medicine scans, MRI scans and ultrasound are all types of diagnostic imaging.

MD80.0.title: Symptom or complaint of the teeth or gum

MD81.title: Abdominal or pelvic pain
MD81.definition: Pain, an unpleasant distress sensation occurring in varying degrees of severity, received by nerve ending in the abdominal and pelvic region.

MD81.10.title: Pain localised to upper abdomen
MD81.10.definition: Pain, an unpleasant distress sensation, which is localised to upper part of abdomen.

MD81.11.title: Pelvic or perineal pain
MD81.11.definition: Pain, an unpleasant distress sensation, which occurs in the pelvic and perineal region.

MD81.12.title: Pain localised to other parts of lower abdomen
MD81.12.definition: Pain, an unpleasant distress sensation, which is localised to other part of lower abdomen than the pelvic or perineal region.

MD81.2.title: Generalised abdominal pain
MD81.2.definition: Pain, an unpleasant distress sensation occurring in varying degrees of severity, or cramps, spasmodic contraction causing severe pain in the abdominal area in general.

MD81.3.title: Acute abdomen
MD81.3.definition: A clinical syndrome with acute abdominal pain that is severe, and rapid onset. Acute abdomen may be caused by a variety of disorders, injuries, or diseases.

MD82.title: Intra-abdominal or pelvic swelling, mass or lump
MD82.definition: This refers to the presence of abdominal or pelvic wall swelling, mass or tumour in the abdominal and pelvic regions. These mass or tumours can be recognised by visual examination and/or palpation.

MD90.title: Nausea or vomiting
MD90.definition: Nausea is the feeling of having an urge to vomit. Vomiting is forcing the contents of the stomach up through the oesophagus and out of the mouth.

MD91.title: Belching
MD91.definition: The liberation of gas in the upper gastrointestinal tract via the oesophagus through the mouth.

MD92.title: Dyspepsia
MD92.definition: A condition characterised by upper abdominal symptoms that suggest indigestion (painful, difficult, or disturbed digestion), which may include pain or discomfort of upper abdomen, bloating, feeling of fullness with very little intake of food, nausea and vomiting, heartburn, loss of appetite.

MD93.title: Dysphagia
MD93.definition: Difficulty in swallowing which may result from neuromuscular disorder or mechanical obstruction. Dysphagia is classified into two distinct types: oropharyngeal dysphagia due to malfunction of the pharynx and upper oesophageal sphincter; and oesophageal dysphagia due to malfunction of the oesophagus.

MD94.title: Halitosis
MD94.definition: Halitosis is an oral health condition in which one's mouth emits a foul odour. There are many causes of halitosis such as poor oral hygiene, tobacco and/or alcohol, and possibly a medical condition such as respiratory and digestive tract disorders.

MD95.title: Heartburn
MD95.definition: Substernal pain or burning sensation, usually associated with regurgitation of gastric juice into the oesophagus.

ME00.title: Abdominal compartment syndrome
ME00.definition: Abdominal compartment syndrome is a condition of organ dysfunction caused by increased intra-abdominal pressure (intra-abdominal hypertension), possibly due to intra-abdominal haemorrhage, retroperitoneal haematoma, or intestinal oedema, often occurred after surgical intervention or trauma, or often associated with septic condition. The importance of this clinical entity was recognised recently in the end of the 20th Century. Usually the abdominal distension due to primary ischaemic bowel injury was excluded from this clinical entity.

ME01.title: Abdominal distension
ME01.definition: This is a condition in which the abdomen feels full and tight because of swelling of the abdomen, usually due to an increased amount of intestinal gas, but occurs sometimes when fluid, substances or mass are accumulating or expanding in the abdomen.

ME02.title: Abdominal rigidity
ME02.definition: Abdominal rigidity is stiffness of the muscles in the belly area, which can be felt when touched or pressed.

ME03.title: Abnormal bowel sounds
ME03.definition: Bowel sounds are caused by the products of digestion as they move through the lower gastrointestinal tract, usually heard on auscultation. Abnormal bowel sounds are reduced or increased bowel sounds which provide valuable information about the disorders of bowel movement.

ME04.title: Ascites
ME04.definition: Accumulation or retention of free fluid in the abdominal peritoneal cavity between the tissues lining the abdomen and abdominal organs. The fluid may be serous, haemorrhagic, or the result of inflammation or tumour metastasis to the peritoneum.

ME05.title: Change in bowel habit
ME05.definition: Bowel habits are the time, size, amount, consistency and frequency of bowel movements throughout the day. A change in bowel habits is any alteration in regular bowel habits.

ME05.0.title: Constipation
ME05.0.definition: Constipation is an acute or chronic condition in which bowel movements occur less often than usual or consist of hard, dry stools that are often painful or difficult to pass. Here constipation other than specifically described elsewhere, such as in motility disorders of intestine or in functional bowel diseases, is described.

ME05.1.title: Diarrhoea
ME05.1.definition: Diarrhoea is an acute or chronic condition in which there is an increased frequency or decreased consistency of bowel movements, usually with excessive and frequent evacuation of watery faeces. Here diarrhoea other than specifically described elsewhere, such as in motility disorders of intestine or in functional bowel diseases, is described.

ME07.title: Faecal incontinence
ME07.definition: Failure of voluntary control of the anal sphincters, with involuntary passage of faeces and flatus.

ME08.title: Flatulence or related conditions
ME08.definition: Production or presence of gas in the gastrointestinal tract which may be expelled through the anus. This category includes also gas induced pain and incontinence of flatus.

ME09.title: Rectal tenesmus
ME09.definition: A symptom, where there is a feeling of constantly needing to pass stools, despite an empty colon.

ME0A.title: Visible peristalsis
ME0A.definition: The wavelike increased peristaltic motions of the intestines by which contents are forced onward toward the opening in such a way that they become visible through the abdominal walls by visual examination.

ME0B.title: Problems with defaecation, not otherwise specified

ME10.0.title: Hepatomegaly or splenomegaly
ME10.0.definition: Hepatomegaly is swelling of the liver beyond its normal size and splenomegaly is an enlargement of the spleen beyond its normal size.

ME10.01.title: Splenomegaly, not elsewhere classified
ME10.01.definition: This refers to swelling of the spleen beyond its normal size, not elsewhere described.

ME10.02.title: Hepatomegaly with splenomegaly
ME10.02.definition: This refers to swelling of the liver and spleen beyond its normal size, not elsewhere described.

ME10.1.title: Unspecified jaundice
ME10.1.definition: A clinical manifestation of hyperbilirubinemia of unspecified origin, characterised by the yellowish staining of the skin; mucus membranes and sclera.
